    "step_2_develop_solution": "<initial_solution>\n### Approach\n\nThe build has four independent parts and one doc edit. It uses stdlib only and adds no new file outside the tests. I read each site on the merged main; line numbers below are from that read.\n\n**R1 \u2014 Client CORS by exact origin.**\n- **Parsing.** `client/backend/server.py` gains a module-level `parse_cors_origins` next to `parse_trusted_proxies`, in the same shape: split on commas, strip each entry, drop empties, return a frozenset. `main()` calls it once, beside the existing `TRUSTED_PROXIES` read and before the signal swap and the bind. It is never read at import or per request.\n- **Storage.** `ClientBackendServer.__init__` gets a trailing `cors_origins` parameter after `trusted_proxies`, defaulting to an empty frozenset, stored as `self.cors_origins`. The constructor already takes seven parameters (trusted_proxies has a default), so the six-argument calls in `tests/active/conftest.py` (both fixtures) and `tests/active/test_server.py:328` keep working with no CORS. `main()` passes the parsed set as the new last argument.\n- **Headers.** `client/backend/lib/http_utils.py` gets one private helper, called by `respond_json`, `respond_bytes` and `respond_options` between `send_response` and `end_headers`, in place of their three or four hard-coded `access-control-*` lines. It reads the request's `Origin` through `getattr(handler, \"headers\", None)` and the configured set through `getattr(getattr(handler, \"server\", None), \"cors_origins\", frozenset())`, so a stub with no server or no headers gets no CORS instead of crashing. It checks exact membership with no normalisation. On a match it sends the echoed allow-origin, `Vary: Origin`, the existing allow-methods and `ALLOWED_REQUEST_HEADERS`, and `access-control-max-age: 600` only when called from `respond_options`. Otherwise it sends nothing.\n- **Invariants.** `respond_options` still always sends 204. Nothing ever sends `allow-credentials`.\n- **Proxied responses.** The Client never copies upstream headers (it re-emits only content-type through `respond_bytes`), so the Engine's headers cannot leak through the proxy.\n\n**R2 \u2014 Engine CORS removed.** In `engine/server/api/http_utils.py`, delete the four `access-control-*` lines from `respond_json` and the four from `respond_options`. `respond_options` stays, still used by `similar.py`, and answers a bare 204. The Engine has no other header site.\n\n**R3 \u2014 Fixed server-error bodies.**\n- **Client, `_proxy_engine_request` (around 685-730).**\n  - The generic branch drops `detail` from its body. Its existing ERROR log already has the error and the traceback.\n  - The transport-unavailable branch drops `detail` from its body, and its log goes from WARNING to ERROR so it meets \"logged at error level\". The log keeps `str(last_transport_error)`.\n  - Both keep `error: \"Engine read proxy failed\"` and their `code`.\n- **Client, the six `EngineApiError` handlers** (resolve 766 and 897, centroids 795, lookup 959, metadata 1015 and 1030): each calls one new private handler method, `_respond_engine_failure(operation, exc)`. It logs through `_emit_client_log` at ERROR, with the operation, the request path and `str(exc)` as context, and answers 502 `{\"error\": f\"Engine {operation} failed\"}`. No traceback is logged, because an `EngineApiError` is an anticipated failure and its text already carries the Engine's error.\n- **Client, bridge publish.** `_publish_to_engine_bridge` is the only producer of `bridge_error`, so the fix goes there, not in the handler. The `URLError`/`TimeoutError` and generic branches log the exception at ERROR through `_emit_client_log`; the generic branch also logs `traceback.format_exc()` because it is unexpected. Both return the fixed `\"engine bridge unavailable\"`. The fixed `engine bridge HTTP {code}` string stays, and so does the activitypub not-implemented string.\n- **Engine, `similar.py` (around 1008-1018).** A `ValueError` in the bad-request set still answers 400 with its own text. Any other `ValueError` gets `logging.exception` and 500 `\"Internal server error\"`. The catch-all keeps its `logging.exception(\"server error\")` and answers the same fixed 500. The bad-request set becomes a module-level named constant instead of a local literal, to match the file's style.\n- **Engine, `internal_events.py` (around 79-81).** The catch-all gets `logging.exception` and a fixed 500. The `ValueError` \u2192 400 path is untouched.\n- **Nothing else needs changing.** I grepped both services for 5xx sites built from `str(exc)` or an f-string with the exception, and these are all of them. `internal_client_reads.py` and `video.py` have only 4xx relays or fixed text. The Client proxy's pass-through of Engine error payloads stays; the Engine's 5xx bodies become fixed at the source.\n\n**R4 \u2014 Debug off by default.**\n- **The flag.** `engine/server/api/server_config.py` gains `_resolve_flag_env(name)` beside the other `_resolve_*_env` helpers. It is true only for `1`, `true` or `yes` after `.strip().lower()`, and false for anything else, empty or unset. `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED = _resolve_flag_env(\"RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG\")` replaces the literal `True`, with its comment updated.\n- **Consumers.** `server.py:56/450` and the `similar.py:922` check are unchanged, and the existing 403 `Debug mode is disabled` covers both routes.\n- **Test fixture.** The `engine` fixture's env in `tests/active/conftest.py` adds `\"RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG\": \"1\"`, so `test_profiles.py`'s `debug.profile` read keeps working.\n\n**R5 \u2014 DEPLOYMENT.md.**\n- **Section 7 (line 416-419).** The quoted constant is replaced by `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1`: off by default, set in the Engine's environment through `.env.bridge` (the Engine unit's `EnvironmentFile`, `engine/install-engine-service.sh:182`) or a systemd drop-in, and it enables `?debug=1` for `/debug.html`.\n- **Section 6 \"Local alternative\".** After the dev-mode block, one paragraph on `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` in the style of the `TRUSTED_PROXIES` paragraph: comma-separated exact origins; unset in production (same-origin through nginx); set to the Vite origin, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, on the Client backend for the cross-origin dev setup; cross-origin dev calls fail until it is set.\n\n**How the acceptance criteria are covered.**\n- **CORS on the Client.** A live Client on an ephemeral port, the same pattern as `client_backend`, built once with no origins and once with `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, is probed with GET and OPTIONS requests that carry each `Origin`.\n- **CORS on the Engine.** A request to the live `engine` fixture, OPTIONS included, checks that no response carries any `access-control-*` header. This test runs in its own `validate_tests.py` invocation because of the Engine rate limit.\n- **Engine metadata failure.** A stdlib stub Engine in the test answers the metadata call with a 500 carrying a distinctive string. The Client's 502 body must not contain it, and the captured log (caplog) must.\n- **Engine recommendations exception.** In an `ENGINE_PY` child, following the `test_similar.py` precedent, a patched method raises a sentinel exception. The body must be the fixed 500 and the child's log must carry the traceback.\n- **Bridge publish failure.** `_publish_to_engine_bridge` is called against a closed port and must return the fixed error while the log carries the exception. A stub Engine that resolves but refuses ingest covers the same thing through the handler.\n- **Debug toggle.** The `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG` values are tested in a child import the way `test_server_config.py` does. `debug=1` \u2192 403 is tested in an `ENGINE_PY` child with the flag off. The live fixture, with the flag on, covers `debug` rows.\n- **Malformed JSON.** Any Client route given a malformed body still answers 400 `Invalid JSON body`.\n\n### Alternatives considered\n\n- **Keeping the origin set in `http_utils`** (a module global set from `main()`) instead of on the server. Rejected: it is hidden process state, tests could not run two Clients with different sets in one interpreter, and the requirements put it on the server.\n- **Passing origins as an explicit argument to `respond_*`.** Rejected: there are about 40 call sites to touch, and the handler already reaches its server.\n- **Echoing the origin plus `Vary: Origin` on every response once any origin is configured.** Rejected: the requirement says no `access-control-*` header without a match, and exact-set echo is what ADR-0004 decides.\n- **Sanitising `bridge_error` in `_handle_user_action` instead of in `_publish_to_engine_bridge`.** Rejected: the raw text would still exist in a return value whose only consumer puts it in a body, so the leak would stay one refactor away.\n- **Inlining the log and respond pair at each of the six `EngineApiError` sites.** Rejected in favour of one private method: six copies of a ten-line `_emit_client_log` call would drift. It is a plain method, not an abstraction.\n- **A generic 500 wrapper in the Engine's `do_GET`/`do_POST`.** Rejected as scope creep. Only the two named handlers leak, and a dispatcher-level catch would change behaviour on every route.\n- **Refusing to start on a malformed `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` entry, the way `TRUSTED_PROXIES` does.** Not done: the settled format only drops empty entries, and a non-origin string is harmless because it never equals a browser's `Origin`.\n\n### Risks and gotchas\n\n- **A literal `*` entry.** If the operator lists `*` and a non-browser client sends `Origin: *`, exact echo would send `access-control-allow-origin: *` and break the \"never `*`\" invariant. The parser therefore drops a `*` entry as well as empty ones. This is the one behaviour beyond the literal parsing text, and it only enforces a stated invariant.\n- **`Origin: null`.** A listed `null` would be echoed to sandboxed frames. That is the operator's explicit choice, and DEPLOYMENT.md will say \"exact origins\" only.\n- **Cache poisoning.** `Vary: Origin` is sent only on a match. With origins configured, a shared cache could store a no-CORS response and serve it to a listed origin. The only configured case is local dev, and nginx does not cache the API, so this is accepted.\n- **Engine fixture env and in-process imports.** The fixture gets the variable in its env copy only, never in the pytest process's `os.environ`. `test_similar.py` imports `server_config` in-process and in `ENGINE_PY` children, so its debug default flips to false; I read that it patches `respond_json` and does not request debug, but the build must confirm it with a run.\n- **Log-level change.** The transport-unavailable log goes from WARNING to ERROR, which changes log volume during an Engine outage. Nothing in the tree filters on that level.\n- **Test stubs.** The only callers that could lack `server` or `headers` are test stubs. The `getattr` defaults cover them, and the Engine helpers read neither.\n- **Engine-backed test runs.** New Engine-backed test files run in their own `validate_tests.py` invocations because of the Engine rate limit. They write to the shared `whitelist.db` only through the existing fixture paths.\n- **Hand-off note.** The Vite cross-origin dev setup fails until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` is set on the Client backend.     "step_4_reassess": "<summary>\nI checked the inventory against the tree: both `http_utils` files, `client/backend/server.py` (constructor, `main()`, `_proxy_engine_request`, the six `EngineApiError` sites, `_publish_to_engine_bridge`), `engine_api_client._post_json`, `similar.py` (`do_OPTIONS`, the outer 503 wrapper, the `_handle_similar` except branches), `internal_events.py`, `server_config.py`, `logging_profiles.py`, `conftest.py`, `dev.mjs`, `api-base.ts`, the videos page's debug switch, DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a76/\u00a77 and the plan's requirements text. Every entry I opened held up, including the inventory's correction that the Engine's `respond_json` has three CORS lines, not four. A grep for `send_response|send_header|send_error|end_headers` shows every response in both services goes through the `respond_*` helpers, so R1/R2 have no bypass site. No shipped HTML sets `data-debug`, so no page asks for debug by default. The plan works for R1, R2, R4 and R5. R3 has one real hole, already in the inventory under `logging_profiles.py`: the running Engine's JSON formatter drops `exc_info`. The plan relies on `logging.exception` for the Engine traceback, so in production R3's traceback requirement and acceptance criterion are not met. The only clean fix touches the log format, which the requirements put out of scope. I report that as a conflict below.\n<question id=\"1\">\n    Mostly yes. R1 fits the code: all three writers call `_finish_response`, which calls `end_headers`, so a helper placed before it works. `handler.headers` / `handler.server` exist on real handlers, and the `getattr` defaults cover the dict-header stub in `test_internal_client_reads.py`. The trailing constructor parameter keeps the three six-argument constructions (`conftest.py:74`, `:161`, `test_server.py:328`) at no CORS. R2 is a clean deletion. R4's fixture line keeps `test_profiles.py:276-279` green. R3 works on the Client side. On the Engine side the bodies become fixed, but the traceback the plan relies on never reaches the production log: `configure_engine_logging` (called at `engine/server/api/server.py:324`) installs `EngineJsonFormatter` as the only handler, and `format` (184-223) reads only `record.getMessage()`. The plan's `ENGINE_PY` child test would pass through `logging.lastResort` while production fails. Two smaller R3 shortfalls are also already in the inventory. First, `_post_json:62-63` wraps unexpected exceptions (e.g. a `JSONDecodeError` from a non-JSON 200) into `EngineApiError`, and the plan logs no traceback for those. Second, the bridge `HTTPError` branch (1049-1050) produces a 502 with nothing logged.\n</question>\n<question id=\"2\">\n    Callers lose diagnostic text. The six frontend `payload.error` displays lose their `: Engine \u2026 (HTTP n): \u2026` suffix, and curl users must read the logs. In production, the Engine-side cause is recorded only if the formatter issue is solved. Every default `npm run dev` session becomes cross-origin (`dev.mjs:84-86` always exports `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:7172`, and `api-base.ts:19-21` prefers it). So the plan's hand-off line that \"the default `npm run dev` path may be unaffected\" is wrong: every dev session breaks until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` is set. The Vite page is normally opened at `http://localhost:5173`, which is a different exact origin from the documented example. Every Engine answers 403 to `debug=1` until opted in, and `pages/videos/index.ts` shows `Debug mode is disabled` instead of rows. Engine outages log at ERROR once per proxied request. Prod and dev units share `.env.bridge` (`install-client-service.sh:196`, `install-engine-service.sh:182`), and `run-services.sh` exports it to both services. So documenting either variable as belonging in that file silently turns it on in production too.\n</question>\n<question id=\"3\">\n    These are needed, beyond the plan's listed edits:\n    - the `engine` fixture env gets `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1`;\n    - CORS tests build their own `ClientBackendServer` with the new argument and read headers through raw `urllib` / `http.client`, because `ClientBackend.request` returns only status and body;\n    - the flag tests strip `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG` from the child env, as `test_server_config.py:24` does for its variable;\n    - the Engine traceback test installs `configure_engine_logging` in its child and asserts on the JSON line, or it proves nothing about production;\n    - the bridge transport test uses a closed port or a direct call, because a refusing stub reaches the `HTTPError` branch the plan does not change;\n    - five docstrings are reworded (Client `http_utils` 34/51/62, Engine `http_utils` 24/37) plus `similar.py:331`;\n    - the hand-off and DEPLOYMENT.md text are corrected as in the recommendations.\n</question>\n<question id=\"4\">\n    CORS:\n    - Client responses carry CORS only for an exact listed origin, now with `Vary: Origin`. Before, every response carried `*`.\n    - The Engine sends no CORS at all, and its OPTIONS is a bare 204.\n\n    5xx bodies:\n    - The Client's 502s drop `detail` and the appended exception text.\n    - `bridge_error` becomes `engine bridge unavailable` for transport and unexpected failures.\n    - A non-bad-request `ValueError` in recommendations, and the recommendations and ingest catch-alls, answer fixed 500s.\n\n    Logging:\n    - The transport-unavailable proxy log moves from WARNING to ERROR.\n    - The `EngineApiError` and bridge failures, which were previously unlogged, now log at ERROR.\n\n    Other changes:\n    - Recommendations debug is off unless `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG` is `1`/`true`/`yes`.\n    - A configured `*` entry is silently dropped.\n\n    Unchanged: statuses, `code` fields, 4xx texts, and the proxy's pass-through of Engine payloads.\n</question>\n</summary>\n\n<new_impacts>\nnone\n</new_impacts>\n\n<unconfirmed>\nnone\n</unconfirmed>\n\n<new_conflicts>\nPlan R3 (Engine) vs requirement R3 and acceptance criterion \"the Engine log carries the traceback\", constrained by Out of scope \"Logging format\". The plan meets the Engine traceback requirement with `logging.exception` in `similar.py` (the existing `logging.exception(\"server error\")` plus a new one for non-bad-request `ValueError`s) and in `internal_events.py`. But the running Engine's only handler is `EngineJsonFormatter` (`engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py:184-238`, installed at `engine/server/api/server.py:324`), and it serialises only `record.getMessage()`, dropping `exc_info`. So once the bodies stop carrying `str(exc)`, the cause of an Engine 500 is recorded nowhere in production. The plan's `ENGINE_PY` test would pass via `logging.lastResort` while production fails. There are two ways to satisfy R3. (a) Put `traceback.format_exc()` into the logged message at those sites. That changes the text of the \"existing `logging.exception(\"server error\")` stays\" call R3 names, or adds a second log call beside it. (b) Have the formatter emit a `traceback` key when `exc_info` is set, which is a logging-format change the requirements put out of scope. The operator must choose which settled text gives.\n</new_conflicts>\n\n<recommendations>\n1. Resolve the conflict with option (a). At the three Engine sites (the `similar.py` non-bad-request `ValueError`, the `similar.py` catch-all, and the `internal_events.py` catch-all), keep `logging.exception(...)` and include the traceback text in the message, e.g. `logging.exception(\"[similar] server error\\n%s\", traceback.format_exc())`, with `import traceback` added to both files. It changes what: about three lines and two imports, no format change, and R3 is met in production. Costs:\n- The \"server error\" message text changes, so the operator must read R3's \"stays\" as \"keeps a `logging.exception` call\".\n- `_extract_fields` may add a few stray `key=value` context entries from the traceback text, which is harmless noise.\n- Under `lastResort` in tests the traceback prints twice.\n- The acceptance test must run `configure_engine_logging` in its `ENGINE_PY` child and assert that the JSON `message` carries the sentinel and `Traceback`.\n\nOption (b), the alternative, is about three lines in `EngineJsonFormatter.format`. It also fixes every other `logging.exception` in the Engine (e.g. `internal_events.py:116`), but it needs the operator to amend \"Logging format\" out of scope, and it adds a key to every error line.\n\n2. In `_respond_engine_failure`, also log `traceback.format_exc()`, at least when `exc.__cause__` is not a `URLError`/`TimeoutError`. It changes what: R3's \"traceback for unexpected ones\" is met for exceptions `_post_json:62-63` wraps (non-JSON 200, `RemoteDisconnected`). Cost: one context key, and larger log lines on those failures only.\n\n3. Log the bridge `HTTPError` branch (`server.py:1049-1050`) at ERROR through `_emit_client_log` with the status. It changes what: the 502 it causes becomes traceable, since today an Engine ingest 5xx leaves no Client log line. Cost: one call and one ERROR line per failed publish. The response is unchanged.\n\n4. Name the `_handle_likes_import` operation \"metadata\", not \"resolve\", because it calls `fetch_metadata_for_entries`. Name the ingest catch-all message `Event ingest failed`, since R3 wants the operation named. Cost: a one-word deviation from how the requirements grouped the site, with no behaviour change.\n\n5. Correct the hand-off and the DEPLOYMENT.md text, at doc-wording cost only:\n- The default `npm run dev` IS cross-origin (`dev.mjs:84-86` plus `api-base.ts:19-21`), so every dev session needs `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS`.\n- Document that the Vite page is usually opened at `http://localhost:5173`, which is a distinct exact origin from `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, and that a `--port 5175` run needs its own entry.\n- Recommend a per-unit systemd drop-in (`systemctl edit peertube-client-dev` / the dev Engine unit) rather than the shared `.env.bridge` for both variables, because prod and dev units, and `run-services.sh`, all read that one file.\n- In \u00a77, point debug at `/videos.html?debug=1` rather than `/debug.html`, which does not exist. Leave the pre-existing line 414 alone, or fix it only if the operator wants it, since the frontend debug page is out of scope.\n\n6. Optional: add the configured origins to the `service.start` log context in `main()`. Cost: one dict key. Benefit: an operator can confirm what is active.\n\n7. Put live-Engine tests (Engine no-CORS, debug rows) in a separate file from the stub and child tests, so they run in their own `validate_tests.py` invocation. Cost: one extra test file and one `config.json` entry at harvest.\n</recommendations>",
    "step_5_draft_implementation": "<draft>\n## Draft implementation: plan 15, tighten response defaults\n\nTwo passes. Pass 1 found one gap. `EngineJsonFormatter`, the only handler in the running Engine, drops `exc_info`, so `logging.exception` would record no traceback in production and R3 plus its acceptance criterion would fail. The operator chose option (b): the formatter adds a `traceback` key. Pass 2 found nothing unmet against the plan or R1-R5. The departures from the high-level plan are listed at the end, each with its reason.\n\nEverything is stdlib, with no new dependency. The only new source file is a test file; the rest are edits.\n\n### What the build must test\n\n| Criterion | Where | Harness |\n|---|---|---|\n| Client CORS: unset \u2192 no allow-origin; listed origin echoed with `Vary: Origin`; preflight methods, headers and max-age; unlisted origin gets nothing; never `*`; OPTIONS always 204 | `test_response_defaults.py` | Two Clients built in the test, with `frozenset()` and with `frozenset({\"http://127.0.0.1:5173\"})`, read through raw `http.client` so headers are visible |\n| `parse_cors_origins` values, including the dropped `*` | same | Pure function |\n| Engine metadata failure \u2192 502 without the Engine's string; Client log has it | same | Stub Engine answering `/internal/videos/metadata` with 500 `{\"error\": \"engine-sentinel-metadata-9c1d\"}`; `POST /api/user-profile/likes` with one `{uuid, host}`; caplog at ERROR |\n| Bridge publish failure \u2192 fixed `bridge_error`; log has the exception | same | `_publish_to_engine_bridge(CLOSED_ENGINE, {...})` called directly; caplog |\n| Malformed JSON \u2192 400 `Invalid JSON body` | same | `POST /api/user-profile/likes` with raw body `{not json` |\n| Recommendations unexpected exception \u2192 fixed 500; Engine log has the traceback | same | `ENGINE_PY` child running `configure_engine_logging`, with `_handle_random` patched to raise a sentinel; stderr parsed as JSON lines |\n| Recommendations `ValueError`: a bad-request text \u2192 400 with that text; any other text \u2192 fixed 500 | same | Same child, more cases |\n| Ingest catch-all \u2192 fixed 500 with a traceback in the log | same | `ENGINE_PY` child; `db_lock` raises `RuntimeError(sentinel)` on enter |\n| Debug flag values | same | `sys.executable` child importing the settled docs checklist |\n\n### Client: `client/backend/lib/http_utils.py`\n\n```python\nALLOWED_REQUEST_HEADERS = \"content-type, x-profile-key\"\nCORS_ALLOWED_METHODS = \"GET, POST, OPTIONS\"\n# Seconds a browser may cache a preflight answer.\nCORS_PREFLIGHT_MAX_AGE = \"600\"\n\n\ndef _send_cors_headers(handler: BaseHTTPRequestHandler, preflight: bool = False) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Send the CORS headers when the request's `Origin` is exactly one the server lists, and none otherwise.\n\n    The origin set is read from `handler.server.cors_origins`, and a handler without a server, headers or that attribute sends none.\n    \"\"\"\n    headers = getattr(handler, \"headers\", None)\n    origin = headers.get(\"Origin\") if headers is not None else None\n    allowed = getattr(getattr(handler, \"server\", None), \"cors_origins\", frozenset())\n    # `*` is refused here as well as in the parser, since a server can be built with any set.\n    if not origin or origin == \"*\" or origin not in allowed:\n        return\n    handler.send_header(\"access-control-allow-origin\", origin)\n    handler.send_header(\"vary\", \"Origin\")\n    handler.send_header(\"access-control-allow-methods\", CORS_ALLOWED_METHODS)\n    handler.send_header(\"access-control-allow-headers\", ALLOWED_REQUEST_HEADERS)\n    if preflight:\n        handler.send_header(\"access-control-max-age\", CORS_PREFLIGHT_MAX_AGE)\n```\n\nThe writers:\n- **`respond_json`**, docstring \"Send a JSON response, with CORS headers for a listed origin.\": `send_response` \u2192 content-type \u2192 `_send_cors_headers(handler)` \u2192 content-length \u2192 `_finish_response`.\n- **`respond_bytes`**, docstring \"Send a non-JSON response payload, with CORS headers for a listed origin.\": same order.\n- **`respond_options`**, docstring \"Answer an OPTIONS request 204, with the preflight CORS headers for a listed origin.\": `send_response(204)` \u2192 `_send_cors_headers(handler, preflight=True)` \u2192 `_finish_response(handler)`.\n\nInvariants:\n- The helper runs before `_finish_response`, so no header is sent after `end_headers`.\n- Only a value equal to an operator-configured entry is echoed.\n- `allow-credentials` is never sent.\n- The helper touches neither `datetime` nor the module's imports, so `test_profiles.py`'s monkeypatch of `http_utils.datetime` is unaffected.\n- A dict-headers stub gets `.get(\"Origin\")` \u2192 None \u2192 no CORS, which is harmless.\n\n### Client: `client/backend/server.py`\n\n**Parser**, placed directly after `parse_trusted_proxies` and before `DEFAULT_TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS`. It is never called at module level.\n```python\ndef parse_cors_origins(value: str) -> frozenset[str]:\n    \"\"\"Parse a `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` value: comma-separated exact origins, each compared to a request's `Origin` as a plain string.\n\n    Whitespace around entries and blank entries are dropped, and so is `*`, which would otherwise be echoed back to a request sending `Origin: *`.\n    \"\"\"\n    entries = (entry.strip() for entry in value.split(\",\"))\n    return frozenset(entry for entry in entries if entry and entry != \"*\")\n```\n\n**Bridge constant**, placed beside the other module constants:\n```python\n# The `bridge_error` of a publish the Engine never answered; the cause goes to the Client log only.\nENGINE_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR = \"engine bridge unavailable\"\n```\n\n**`ClientBackendServer.__init__`**: a trailing `cors_origins: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),` after `trusted_proxies`, and `self.cors_origins = cors_origins` after `self.trusted_proxies = trusted_proxies`. The existing six-argument constructions keep their default of no CORS.\n\n**`main()`**: directly after the `TRUSTED_PROXIES` try/except, before `logging.basicConfig`:\n```python\n    cors_origins = parse_cors_origins(os.environ.get(\"CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS\", \"\"))\n```\n- `ClientBackendServer(...)` gains `cors_origins,` after `trusted_proxies,`.\n- The `service.start` context gains `\"cors_origins\": sorted(cors_origins),`, so an operator can see which origins are active.\n\n**`_proxy_engine_request`**:\n- Generic branch: the body becomes `{\"error\": \"Engine read proxy failed\", \"code\": \"ENGINE_PROXY_FAILURE\"}`. Its log is unchanged: it is already at ERROR and carries `str(exc)` and the traceback.\n- Transport-unavailable tail: `_emit_client_log(logging.ERROR, ...)` in place of `logging.WARNING`, with the same context. The body becomes `{\"error\": \"Engine read proxy failed\", \"code\": \"ENGINE_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE\"}`.\n\n**New handler method**, placed after `_handle_user_profile_likes_from_client`:\n```python\n    def _respond_engine_failure(self, operation: str, exc: EngineApiError) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Log a failed Engine call with its cause at error level and answer 502 naming only the operation, so no Engine error text reaches the caller.\n\n        Call it only inside the `except EngineApiError` block, where `traceback.format_exc()` still sees the exception.\n        \"\"\"\n        context: dict[str, Any] = {\"operation\": operation, \"path\": self.path, \"error\": str(exc)}\n        cause = exc.__cause__\n        # A cause other than a transport failure is unexpected, e.g. a non-JSON 200 or a dropped connection, and its traceback is the only record of it.\n        if cause is not None and not isinstance(cause, (URLError, TimeoutError)):\n            context[\"traceback\"] = traceback.format_exc()\n        _emit_client_log(logging.ERROR, \"engine.call\", f\"engine {operation} failed\", context)\n        respond_json(self, 502, {\"error\": f\"Engine {operation} failed\"})\n```\n\nCall sites. Each `respond_json(self, 502, {\"error\": f\"Engine \u2026 failed: {exc}\"})` becomes `self._respond_engine_failure(\"<op>\", exc)` and keeps the `return` after it.\n\n| Handler | Site | Operation |\n|---|---|---|\n| `_handle_user_action` | resolve | `\"resolve\"` |\n| `_handle_user_action` | `_store_reaction` | `\"centroids\"` |\n| `_handle_likes_import` | `fetch_metadata_for_entries` | `\"metadata\"` (was \"resolve\"; this is the call it makes) |\n| `_handle_block_add` | resolve and metadata | `\"lookup\"` |\n| `_handle_user_profile_likes_get` | metadata | `\"metadata\"` |\n| `_handle_user_profile_likes_from_client` | metadata | `\"metadata\"` |\n\n**`_publish_to_engine_bridge`**:\n```python\n    except HTTPError as exc:\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"error\": f\"engine bridge HTTP {exc.code}\"}\n    except (URLError, TimeoutError) as exc:\n        _emit_client_log(logging.ERROR, \"engine.bridge\", \"bridge publish unavailable\", {\"event_id\": payload.get(\"event_id\"), \"error\": str(exc)})\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"error\": ENGINE_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR}\n    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover\n        _emit_client_log(logging.ERROR, \"engine.bridge\", \"bridge publish exception\", {\"event_id\": payload.get(\"event_id\"), \"error\": str(exc), \"traceback\": traceback.format_exc()})\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"error\": ENGINE_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR}\n```\n- `_publish_event`'s activitypub string is unchanged.\n- The consumer in `_handle_user_action` is unchanged; it now only ever receives fixed strings.\n- `URLError`, `traceback` and `Any` are already imported in server.py.\n- `engine_api_client.py` is not touched, so the `EngineApiError` text, which carries the Engine's error string, reaches the log intact.\n\n### Engine: `engine/server/api/http_utils.py`\n\n- **`respond_json`**: delete the three `access-control-*` lines. The fixture sets `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1`, so this proves env \u2192 `server_config` \u2192 `main()` \u2192 gate end to end.\n\n### Docs\n\nThese follow the settled checklist:\n- **DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a77**: `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1`, off by default, `1`/`true`/`yes` in any case, 403 `Debug mode is disabled` otherwise. Point at `/videos.html?debug=1`, not `/debug.html`. Prefer a per-unit drop-in over the shared `.env.bridge`.\n- **DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a76**: a `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` paragraph:\n  - exact origins; whitespace, blank entries and `*` are ignored;\n  - unset in production;\n  - `npm run dev` always targets `http://127.0.0.1:7172`, so default dev is cross-origin and needs this;\n  - `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are distinct entries, and `--port 5175` needs its own;\n  - a change needs a restart.\n- **DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a73b**: the `Engine metadata failed` symptom (the HTTP status is now only in `journalctl`).\n- **Triage rows**, optional.\n- **The three READMEs**, as listed in the checklist.\n- No file quotes the `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED = True` constant any more.\n\n### Departures from the high-level plan\n\n1. **Engine formatter gains a `traceback` key.** This is operator decision (b). Without it, R3's \"Engine log carries the traceback\" is false in production.\n2. **`_respond_engine_failure` logs a traceback when the `EngineApiError` wraps a non-transport cause.** The plan said no traceback. `_post_json` wraps unexpected exceptions (a non-JSON 200, `RemoteDisconnected`) into `EngineApiError`, and R3 wants a traceback for unexpected ones. Transport failures and HTTP-status failures stay traceback-free.\n3. **The likes-import operation word is `metadata`, not `resolve`**, because that is the call it makes.\n4. **The recommendations 500 message is `Recommendations request failed`, not `Internal server error`.** R3 requires the message to name the operation. The ingest message is `Event ingest failed` for the same reason.\n5. **`_send_cors_headers` also refuses `Origin: *`**, as well as the parser dropping it. The constructor accepts any set, so the invariant is enforced where the header is sent.\n\n### Deliberate simplifications and known limits\n\n- **Exact-string origin match with no normalisation.** Ceiling: `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` need separate entries. Upgrade path: normalise both sides in the parser and the helper.\n- **Origin set fixed for the process's life.** A change needs a restart, as with `TRUSTED_PROXIES`.\n- **`Vary: Origin` only on a match.** With origins configured, a shared cache could serve a no-CORS response to a listed origin. This is accepted, since only local dev configures origins and nginx does not cache the API.\n- **Not changed, by the plan's scope:**\n  - The proxy HTTPError-without-payload branch still logs an upstream 5xx at WARNING.\n  - `ENGINE_PROXY_INVALID` still logs nothing.\n  - The bridge `engine bridge HTTP {code}` path still logs nothing.\n  - All three bodies are already fixed text, and the Engine side logs its own 5xx with a traceback now. Raising these log levels is a follow-up if a strict reading of R3's logging clause is wanted.\n- **Debug 403 without the variable is proven through an `ENGINE_PY` child**, which uses the imported `server_config` flag in a stub server. `main()`'s env-to-server wiring is proven only by the flag-on live test.\n- **Pre-existing timeout behaviour.** An `OperationalError('interrupted')` inside `_handle_similar` or ingest still lands in the catch-all as a 500. It now has a fixed body and a logged traceback.\n\n### Hand-off notes\n\n- The Vite dev setup, including plain `npm run dev`, which always sets `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:7172`, gets no API access until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` lists the page's exact origin.\n- `/videos.html?debug=1` shows `Debug mode is disabled` until the Engine runs with `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1`.\n- Neither variable should go in the shared `.env.bridge` on a host that also runs prod units; use a per-unit drop-in.\n- Run `test_engine_response_defaults.py` in its own `validate_tests.py` invocation, because of the Engine rate limit.\n- At harvest, add both new test files to `.un/skills/devsecops/config.json` and map `logging_profiles.py`.\n</draft>",
    "step_6_develop_phase_breakdown": "<phases>\n<phase n=\"1\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>Seam 1 is `parse_cors_origins` as a pure function: \"\" \u2192 empty; \" http://a:1 , ,http://b \" \u2192 {\"http://a:1\", \"http://b\"}; \"*, http://a\" \u2192 {\"http://a\"}; \",,\" \u2192 empty. Seam 2 is the HTTP boundary of a live Client. The test builds two `ClientBackendServer`s on ephemeral ports over a tmp users.db, the same construction as the `client_backend` fixture in tests/active/conftest.py plus the trailing `cors_origins` argument: one with frozenset() and one with frozenset({\"http://127.0.0.1:5173\"}). Both are read through raw `http.client` so every header is visible. Assertions: (a) With the empty set, GET /api/health and OPTIONS /api/user-profile carry no header starting `access-control-`, whatever the Origin, and OPTIONS is 204. (b) With the listed set, Origin http://127.0.0.1:5173 on a GET gets allow-origin echoed, `vary: Origin`, methods \"GET, POST, OPTIONS\", headers \"content-type, x-profile-key\", no max-age and no allow-credentials. (c) The same Origin on OPTIONS gets 204, the same headers, and max-age \"600\". (d) Origins http://localhost:5173, https://evil.example and `*` get no access-control-* header on GET or OPTIONS, and OPTIONS is still 204. (e) The 401 from GET /api/user-profile (respond_json) and the 204 from POST /api/profile/delete (respond_bytes) carry the echo. (f) No header value in any of these responses equals `*`.</checkpoint>\n<name>Client CORS by exact origin</name>\n<intent>The Client backend sends CORS headers only to a request whose Origin exactly matches the set that `parse_cors_origins` builds from CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS in `main()` and that `ClientBackendServer` holds as `cors_origins`.</intent>\n<clause_1>`parse_cors_origins` turns a CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS value into a frozenset of exact origins, dropping surrounding whitespace, blank entries and `*`.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>`respond_json`, `respond_bytes` and `respond_options` send access-control-* headers only when the request's Origin is in `server.cors_origins`: they echo that Origin with `Vary: Origin`, and they add max-age 600 only on the 204 preflight.</clause_2>\n<files>client/backend/lib/http_utils.py (EDITED), client/backend/server.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_response_defaults.py (NEW)</files>\n</phase>\n<phase n=\"2\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>Seam 1 is `server_config` imported in a `sys.executable` child with a controlled environment, following the `_run` pattern in tests/active/test_server_config.py. RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG set to 1, true, yes, TRUE or \" yes \" gives RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED True. Unset, \"\", 0, no or on gives False. Seam 2 is an ENGINE_PY child with RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG removed from its env, following tests/active/test_similar.py. It calls `_handle_similar` with params {\"debug\": [\"1\"]} on a stub server whose recommendations_debug_enabled comes from the imported server_config, and asserts respond_json receives [403, {\"error\": \"Debug mode is disabled\"}]. Seam 3 is the live `engine` fixture in tests/active/conftest.py, whose env now includes RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1. The test lives in tests/active/test_engine_response_defaults.py and runs in its own validate_tests.py invocation. Raw http.client requests with Origin http://127.0.0.1:5173 to GET /api/health, OPTIONS /recommendations (which answers 204) and POST /recommendations carry no header starting `access-control-`. POST /recommendations?debug=1&limit=3 answers 200, and every row has a `debug` key. The existing test_profiles.py debug.profile read stays green.</checkpoint>\n<name>Engine CORS off, debug opt-in</name>\n<intent>The Engine sends no CORS header on any response, and it returns recommendation debug metadata only when its environment sets RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG to 1, true or yes.</intent>\n<clause_1>No Engine response, OPTIONS included, carries a header starting `access-control-`.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED is true only when RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG, stripped and lower-cased, is 1, true or yes; otherwise a debug=1 recommendations request answers 403.</clause_2>\n<files>engine/server/api/http_utils.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/server_config.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py (EDITED), tests/active/conftest.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_engine_response_defaults.py (NEW), tests/active/test_response_defaults.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n<phase n=\"3\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>Seam 1 is the Client's HTTP boundary with a stub Engine. A stdlib BaseHTTPRequestHandler stub answers /internal/videos/metadata with 500 {\"error\": \"engine-sentinel-metadata-9c1d\"}. A Client is built over that stub as in phase 1's harness. With caplog at ERROR, POST /api/user-profile/likes sends {\"likes\": [{\"uuid\": \"u1\", \"host\": \"h.example\"}]}. It must answer 502 with body exactly {\"error\": \"Engine metadata failed\"}, and the sentinel must be absent from the raw body. The sentinel must appear in caplog.text, and some ERROR record's JSON must have event \"engine.call\". Seam 2 is `_publish_to_engine_bridge` called directly against a closed port. It returns {\"ok\": False, \"error\": \"engine bridge unavailable\"}, and an ERROR record with event \"engine.bridge\" carries a non-empty context.error that differs from the fixed text. Regression guard: POST /api/user-profile/likes with the raw body `{not json` still answers 400 {\"error\": \"Invalid JSON body\"}.</checkpoint>\n<name>Client fixed failure bodies</name>\n<intent>A failed Engine call or bridge publish now answers the Client's caller with fixed text that names the operation, and the failure's cause is recorded only in the Client log at ERROR.</intent>\n<clause_1>The 502 bodies for Engine-call failures and the `bridge_error` from a failed bridge publish carry only fixed text naming the operation, never the Engine's or the exception's text.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>The Client log records the failure's cause (the Engine's error text or the transport exception) at ERROR level.</clause_2>\n<files>client/backend/server.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_response_defaults.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n<phase n=\"4\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>The seam is ENGINE_PY children that run the production `configure_engine_logging(\"verbose\")` from logging_profiles, following the ENGINE_PY child pattern in tests/active/test_similar.py, with stderr parsed as JSON lines. Similar child, with respond_json patched: `_handle_random` raising RuntimeError(\"sentinel-boom-4e2b\") answers [500, {\"error\": \"Recommendations request failed\"}]. Raising ValueError(\"sentinel-value-8a1c\") gives the same 500. Raising ValueError(\"Vector norm is zero\") answers [400, {\"error\": \"Vector norm is zero\"}]. Stderr has an ERROR line whose `traceback` contains \"Traceback\" and sentinel-boom-4e2b, and another whose traceback contains sentinel-value-8a1c. Ingest child: read_json_body is patched to return one event, and db_lock raises RuntimeError(\"sentinel-ingest-5d7e\") on enter. The result is a single [500, {\"error\": \"Event ingest failed\"}] call, and the stderr JSON `traceback` contains the sentinel.</checkpoint>\n<name>Engine fixed 500s with logged traceback</name>\n<intent>The Engine's recommendations and ingest handlers answer an unexpected failure with a fixed 500 naming the operation, and `EngineJsonFormatter` writes that failure's traceback to the Engine log.</intent>\n<clause_1>`_handle_similar` and the ingest handler answer any failure outside the bad-request set with a fixed 500 body naming the operation, while a ValueError whose text is in SIMILAR_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS still answers 400 with that text.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>A `logging.exception` record rendered by EngineJsonFormatter carries a `traceback` key holding the exception's traceback.</clause_2>\n<files>engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/handlers/internal_events.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_response_defaults.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n</phases>\n\n<needs_coordination>\nNo phase needs a credential or a manual step. The checkpoints for phases 2 and 4 run ENGINE_PY children and need the Engine pixi environment installed locally at engine/.pixi/envs/default/bin/python. Phase 2's live-Engine checkpoint, tests/active/test_engine_response_defaults.py, must run in its own validate_tests.py invocation because of the Engine rate limit.\n</needs_coordination>\n\n<rationale>\nThe build splits along the four settled requirements, turned into four seams, and each Intent reduces to two clauses. R1 (Client CORS) is its own phase: parsing in one clause, gated header emission in the other. R2 and R4 share a phase because both are Engine response defaults and are proven through the same Engine harnesses: server_config child imports, an ENGINE_PY child, and the live `engine` fixture, whose env change (RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1) must land together with the flag so that test_profiles.py stays green. R3 is split by service. Its Client half (fixed 502 and bridge_error text plus ERROR logging) is proven at the Client HTTP boundary with a stub Engine and caplog. Its Engine half (fixed 500s plus the formatter's traceback key, operator decision (b)) is proven in ENGINE_PY children running the production formatter. One R3 phase would have carried three or more facts across two services and two harnesses. R5 and the README edits are documentation, so they get no phase and are left to Step 9. The malformed-JSON 400 criterion is unchanged behaviour, so it sits in phase 3's checkpoint as a regression guard rather than as a clause. The step's {principles}, {shape_ladder-ladder} and {tdd_seams} placeholders arrived unfilled, so the seams were placed on the harnesses the tree already uses (the conftest fixtures, the test_similar.py ENGINE_PY children and the test_server_config.py `_run` pattern), which I confirmed by reading tests/active. The operator approved this breakdown unchanged.\n</rationale>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py": "<items>\n<item id=\"C2c\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>test_error_and_bytes_responses_echo_listed_origin now mints one key and sends POST /api/profile/blocks/remove, which answers 204 through `respond_bytes` (server.py:981), once with each of SECOND and the six UNLISTED Origins: http://localhost:5173, HTTP://127.0.0.1:5173, http://127.0.0.1:5173/, https://evil.example, `*`, and no Origin. :196 asserts `_cors(...) == {}` for every unlisted one, and :195 asserts each is still 204. In the same test, :192 and :193 assert that SECOND is echoed with `Vary: Origin` on that same route, which is the positive control. :203 adds all of these responses to the no-`*` check. It excludes three wrong versions of `respond_bytes`: one that echoes whatever Origin arrives (evil.example would read `{allow-origin: [https://evil.example], \u2026}`), one that falls back to `*` when no Origin is sent (it would read `{allow-origin: ['*'], \u2026}`), and one that still sends `*` unconditionally. I use block-remove instead of repeated deletes because each delete needs its own key, and minting is capped at 5 per hour (PROFILE_MINT_MAX_REQUESTS, server.py:64). Seven Origins would hit that cap. Removing a block that was never added is a repeatable 204: probe_bytes_path.py showed 204, octet-stream, empty body for four Origins with one key. The docstring gets one bullet that says this.</what>\n</item>\n</items>\n\n<findings_addressed>\nClaim CRITICAL 1 (whole-claim, `respond_bytes` has only its positive half): fixed as C2c above. Every unlisted Origin, and a request with no Origin, now reaches `respond_bytes` through POST /api/profile/blocks/remove and is asserted to get no access-control-* headers at :196. The listed SECOND on the same route and in the same test is echoed at :192/:193.\nShape CRITICAL 1 (absence-only in test_unlisted_origin_gets_no_cors_headers): the same BOTH Client now answers LISTED on GET /api/health and OPTIONS /api/user-profile first. Those are asserted equal to `_echo(LISTED)` and `_preflight_echo(LISTED)` at :169/:170, before any unlisted Origin is read. A helper that never emits headers, or whose membership check is always false, now fails there.\nShape CRITICAL 2 (absence-only in test_no_listed_origin_sends_no_cors_headers): the test first starts a Client that holds BOTH over the same tmp db. It asserts that LISTED is echoed on GET (:130) and on the preflight (:131), and only then starts the empty-set Client and asserts nothing is sent for that same LISTED Origin. The empty result is now a difference between two configurations, not silence.\nClaim RECOMMENDATION 1 (near-miss Origins), taken: I added HTTP://127.0.0.1:5173 and http://127.0.0.1:5173/ to UNLISTED, so every negative GET, OPTIONS and bytes assertion checks them. A case-insensitive or slash-normalising match now fails. probe_bytes_path.py showed that http.client sends both values verbatim.\nClaim RECOMMENDATION 2 (`*` variants), taken in part: I added parser cases `\"*\"` \u2192 frozenset() and `\" * ,http://a\"` \u2192 {\"http://a\"}. I did not add a wildcard-pattern case such as `http://*.example`, because C1 says only that `*` is dropped and does not say whether a pattern entry is kept.\n</findings_addressed>\n\n<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py:107 \u2014 `parse_cors_origins(value)` is a frozenset; :108 \u2014 it equals the expected set, for \"\", \" http://a:1 , ,http://b \", \"*, http://a\", \",,\", \"*\", \" * ,http://a\"</assertion>\n<expected>frozenset() for \"\", \",,\" and \"*\"; {\"http://a:1\", \"http://b\"} for the whitespace/blank case; {\"http://a\"} for both `*` cases.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A parser that returns a set or list fails :107. One that splits without stripping reads {\" http://a:1 \", \"\", \"http://b \"}. One that keeps blanks reads {\"\"} for \",,\". One that drops only a bare leading \"*\" keeps \"*\" from \" * ,http://a\". Each of these fails :108.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>:152, :158, :198, :201, :192 echo exactly allow-origin/methods/headers, with max-age only on the preflight (:153, :154, :158), and `vary == [\"Origin\"]` at :155, :159, :193, :199, :202, for json GET, the options preflight, the json 401 and the bytes 204s. For absence, the same Client with LISTED echoed first gives `_cors == {}` for unlisted, near-miss, `*` and absent Origins on json (:174), options (:178) and bytes (:196), and the empty set gives `{}` for LISTED at :137/:141 against its BOTH control at :130/:131. No `*` value appears anywhere (:143, :161, :180, :203).</assertion>\n<expected>Listed Origin: the Origin itself, \"GET, POST, OPTIONS\", \"content-type, x-profile-key\", plus [\"600\"] only on OPTIONS 204, with Vary [\"Origin\"] once. Any other Origin, or an empty set: no access-control-* header, and the status stays 200/204/401/204.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>Keeping `*` reads allow-origin ['*'] at :130/:152/:169/:192. Echoing any Origin reads the evil or near-miss Origin at :174/:178/:196. A case-insensitive or slash-normalising match echoes HTTP://127.0.0.1:5173 or http://127.0.0.1:5173/ at :174. Fixing only json/options leaves `*` or an echo on bytes at :196. An allow-list read from env or a module global ignores the server attribute and differs between :130 and :137. Emitting max-age on every response fails :153 and the exact-dict :192/:201. Doubling Vary reads [\"Origin\", \"Origin\"].</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Absence only: before the edits, yes, in the two tests the shape auditor named and in the new bytes negatives. Rewritten: every absence assertion now sits in a test that first asserts a listed echo on the same routes, at :130/:131, :169/:170 and :192. Deleting the CORS emission turns those controls red.\n2. Echoed literal: no. `_echo` and `_preflight_echo` are fixed literals and are not computed from production. Deleting the `send_header(\"access-control-allow-origin\", origin)` echo in any of the three helpers turns :152, :158 or :192 red.\n3. One value: no. The echo is read for two listed Origins, so a hard-coded origin fails. Absence is read for six unlisted values, including two near-misses. The bytes path is read for listed and unlisted Origins on the same route.\n4. The double: none. Every test runs a real ClientBackendServer over a real sqlite db. `cors_origins` is set on the real server object, and the only other object built is a real RateLimiter.\n5. It collects: yes. The run collected 11 items: 6 parser cases and 5 tests. `_raw` gained a `body` parameter, and every caller matches it.\n6. Observed, not predicted: yes. probe_bytes_path.py showed blocks/remove answering 204 through the octet-stream path for four Origins on one key, 400 on an empty body (which is why BLOCK_REMOVE is sent), and http.client sending HTTP://127.0.0.1:5173 and http://127.0.0.1:5173/ verbatim. The run of the test confirmed that the block-remove status assertion at :191 passes on today's code.\n7. Still red for its own reason: yes. The 6 parser cases fail with AttributeError (no `parse_cors_origins`). The constructor test fails with a TypeError on the 8th positional argument. The four HTTP tests fail at :130, :152, :169 and :192, where allow-origin reads ['*'] and not the listed Origin. None of them fail in the harness. I have no delete tool, so tests/tmp/probe_bytes_path.py and tests/tmp/probe_cors_headers.py are still on disk and need removing. Neither matches `test_*.py`.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "self_check:tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py": "<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py:100 and :101 \u2014 for each of \"\", \" http://a:1 , ,http://b \", \"*, http://a\" and \",,\", `parse_cors_origins(value)` is a frozenset (100) and equals the expected set exactly (101)</assertion>\n<expected>\"\" \u2192 frozenset(); \" http://a:1 , ,http://b \" \u2192 frozenset({\"http://a:1\", \"http://b\"}); \"*, http://a\" \u2192 frozenset({\"http://a\"}); \",,\" \u2192 frozenset(). The run shows AttributeError at :99 because the function does not exist yet.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A parser that copies `parse_trusted_proxies`: it strips but keeps `*` and reads {\"*\", \"http://a\"}; or it falls back to a default on an empty value and reads non-empty for \"\" and \",,\". One that also sends max-age on non-preflight responses fails :140, since the comparison is exact equality.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py:141, :142, :143 and :147 \u2014 the listed-origin GET has no access-control-max-age (141) and no access-control-allow-credentials (142); both the GET and the preflight carry `vary` exactly once as [\"Origin\"] (143, 147)</assertion>\n<expected>max-age and allow-credentials are absent from the GET. vary == [\"Origin\"] on the GET and on the preflight. :146 in the same loop is the positive control that max-age does arrive on the preflight.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>An echo with no Vary header reads None at :143. One that opts into credentials fails :142.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py:125, :128, :129 and :131 \u2014 a Client with an empty cors_origins answers GET /api/health and OPTIONS /api/user-profile, for Origin http://127.0.0.1:5173, http://localhost:5173, https://evil.example, `*` and no Origin, with no access-control-* header (125, 129), OPTIONS is 204 (128), and no header value is `*` (131)</assertion>\n<expected>_cors(headers) == {} on every response, and every OPTIONS status is 204. _star_values over all ten responses is []. The status asserts at :124/:128 show each request reached the handler.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>The current code, observed: the run failed at :125 for http://127.0.0.1:5173 with {'access-control-allow-origin': ['*'], allow-methods, allow-headers}. So does one that treats an empty set as \"allow all\".</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py:158, :161, :162 and :164 \u2014 the Client listing BOTH answers http://localhost:5173, https://evil.example, `*` and no Origin with no access-control-* header on GET (158) and OPTIONS (162), OPTIONS is still 204 (161), and no value is `*` (164)</assertion>\n<expected>_cors(headers) == {} and OPTIONS 204 for all four unlisted cases; _star_values == []. The positive control that this server does emit CORS for a listed origin is :140/:146 in the sibling test, built with the same set.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>The current code, observed: the run failed at :158 for http://localhost:5173 with allow-origin ['*']. Matching by host or prefix instead of exact string equality would echo http://localhost:5173 or `*`. So would a helper that sends CORS whenever the set is non-empty.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py:174, :175, :177, :178 and :179 \u2014 the 401 from GET /api/user-profile with Origin http://127.0.0.1:5173 (respond_json) and the 204 from POST /api/profile/delete with Origin https://dev.example:8443 (respond_bytes) each carry exactly that origin's echo and vary [\"Origin\"], and neither has a `*` value</assertion>\n<expected>refused: _cors == _echo(\"http://127.0.0.1:5173\"), vary [\"Origin\"]. deleted: _cors == _echo(\"https://dev.example:8443\"), vary [\"Origin\"]. No `*`. The statuses 401/201/204 at :173/:171/:176 match what the probe observed on the current code.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>The current code, observed: the run failed at :174 with allow-origin ['*'] against ['http://127.0.0.1:5173']. An implementation that changes only respond_options, or only respond_json, leaves respond_bytes sending the wildcard, which fails :177. One that gives respond_bytes no helper sends no echo and fails :177 as well.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Whole claim: before this turn, no. The HTTP tests could not reach any C2 assertion, and the echo was tested at one listed origin only. After the rewrite, yes. C1 is carried by :100-101 over four inputs. C2's clauses are carried as follows:\n- echo only for a listed Origin: :140/:146 against :125/:129/:158/:162;\n- Vary: Origin: :143/:147/:175/:178;\n- max-age only on the 204 preflight: :141 against :146, with 204 at :128/:145/:161;\n- all three writers: respond_json via /api/health and the 401, respond_bytes via the delete 204, respond_options via OPTIONS;\n- never `*`: :131/:149/:164/:179.\nThe docstring's constructor claim, not a clause, is carried by test_server_holds_trailing_cors_origins (:108-112). Not gated here: main() reading CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS. That is in the Intent but not in C1 or C2.\n\n2. Absence only: yes, before the rewrite. Every HTTP test built the server with `cors_origins=`, which raised TypeError, so the `_cors(...) == {}` and `not in` assertions were never reached. Rewritten as follows:\n- `_client` builds the six-argument server and sets `srv.cors_origins`, the attribute the helpers read per the plan.\n- The negatives are now reached, and each has a control. Status asserts at :124/:128/:157/:161 show the handler ran. The listed test (:140/:146), built with the same BOTH set, shows the server does emit CORS. :146 arms :141.\n- _star_values is armed by the observed current output, which carries '*'.\n\n3. Echoed literal: no. The expected origin is the request's Origin, and the server must copy it into a response header. Deleting the `send_header(\"access-control-allow-origin\", origin)` line of the new helper turns :140/:174/:177 red. The test performs no transformation production does.\n\n4. One value: yes, before the rewrite. The echo was read at a single listed origin, so \"send the configured origin\" was indistinguishable from \"echo the request Origin\". Rewritten: the listed set is BOTH = {http://127.0.0.1:5173, https://dev.example:8443}, and the listed test loops over both (:137). The respond_bytes path uses the second origin (:172, :177). The parser is read at four inputs.\n\n5. Double: no. Everything is the real ClientBackendServer, real handler and real http_utils over a real sqlite file. Setting the `cors_origins` attribute is configuration of the real object, not a stand-in.\n\n6. It collects: yes. The run printed \"collected 9 items\": 4 parser params plus 5 functions. Every import resolves, and `DEFAULT_TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS` exists at server.py:167. The failures are AttributeError, TypeError and AssertionError, with no ImportError or NameError. The earlier `--collect-only` output said \"no tests\", but the full run collected 9.\n\n7. Observed, not predicted: these values come from the probe on the current code (tests/tmp/probe_cors_headers.py, output read from tests/last_test_output.txt) and from this run:\n- statuses 200/204/401/201/204, and the 201 body's `key`;\n- lower-case header names;\n- no Vary header today;\n- http.client sends `Origin: *` verbatim;\n- the current wildcard values.\nSome values can only be observed once the phase exists: the echoed allow-origin, `vary: Origin` and max-age \"600\" on a match. They are the requirement's R1 literals (methods and headers match today's observed values), not guesses about an output shape. Implementing the phase and running this file would confirm them. I could not delete the probe (no delete tool), so I overwrote it with a one-line comment asking for its removal. pytest does not collect it.\n\n8. Red, not green: red. The ValidateTests run printed \"9 failed\" and \"recorded: tests/last_test_validation.json (exit 1)\" with \"[exit status 1]\".\n\n9. Red for the right reason: yes. Each failure is the phase's own missing behaviour or interface, and no control assertion failed:\n- The 4 parser cases fail at :99: \"AttributeError: module 'server' has no attribute 'parse_cors_origins'\". That is the C1 function itself.\n- test_server_holds_trailing_cors_origins fails at :108: \"TypeError: ClientBackendServer.__init__() takes from 7 to 8 positional arguments but 9 were given\". That is the missing trailing parameter.\n- test_no_listed_origin_sends_no_cors_headers fails at :125: \"AssertionError: http://127.0.0.1:5173\", Left contains {'access-control-allow-origin': ['*'], ...}. The status control at :124 passed first.\n- test_listed_origins_are_echoed_with_vary_and_preflight_max_age fails at :140: {'access-control-allow-origin': ['*']} != {'access-control-allow-origin': ['http://127.0.0.1:5173']}.\n- test_unlisted_origin_gets_no_cors_headers fails at :158: \"AssertionError: http://localhost:5173\", allow-origin ['*'].\n- test_error_and_bytes_responses_echo_listed_origin fails at :174: ['*'] != ['http://127.0.0.1:5173']. The :171 control (201) passed before it.\n\n10. Observed expected output: each row's `expected` is the value under the right implementation, and each row's wrong_implementation quotes what this run actually showed. The run showed the wildcard allow-origin ['*'] with allow-methods ['GET, POST, OPTIONS'] and allow-headers ['content-type, x-profile-key']. Those two values equal the unchanged parts of the expected echo, so the run confirms them. The run contradicted no row. The only unobservable parts are the echoed origin, vary and max-age on a match (see 7).\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:1": "<changes>\n### `client/backend/lib/http_utils.py`\n- New private `_send_cors_headers(handler, preflight=False)`. It reads the request's `Origin` from the handler. If that Origin is exactly in `handler.server.cors_origins`, it sends: `access-control-allow-origin` set to that Origin, the existing allow-methods (`GET, POST, OPTIONS`) and allow-headers (`content-type, x-profile-key`), `access-control-max-age: 600` only when `preflight` is true, and `vary: Origin`. For any other Origin, or none, it sends no `access-control-*` header and no `Vary`.\n- `respond_json` and `respond_bytes` no longer hard-code `access-control-allow-origin: *` and the allow-* headers. They call `_send_cors_headers(handler)` instead.\n- `respond_options` still answers 204 but now calls `_send_cors_headers(handler, preflight=True)`, so max-age goes out only alongside an echoed Origin. Nothing in this module sends `*` any more.\n\n### `client/backend/server.py`\n- New `parse_cors_origins(value) -> frozenset[str]`, placed next to `parse_trusted_proxies`. It splits on commas, trims whitespace, and drops blank entries and `*`. Matching is exact: no case folding and no trailing-slash normalisation. A value listing nothing gives the empty set, so no origin is allowed.\n- `ClientBackendServer.__init__` takes a new trailing argument, `cors_origins: frozenset[str] = frozenset()`, after `trusted_proxies`, and stores it as `self.cors_origins`. The existing six-argument construction (as in conftest's `client_backend`) holds the empty set.\n- `main()` parses `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` from the environment right after `TRUSTED_PROXIES`, before the signal swap and the DB/bind, and passes the result to `ClientBackendServer`.\n- For the hand-off: once this lands, the Vite dev setup gets no CORS headers until the Client backend is started with `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` set to the Vite origin (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:5173`). This is by design under ADR-0004, and `DEPLOYMENT.md` documents it in a later phase.\n\n### `tests/active/test_response_defaults.py`\nNot created here. The phase list names it as NEW, but this step asks only for the production code behind the checkpoint `tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py`. The durable test is expected to be promoted from that checkpoint by the workflow.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

    "step_7_implement:2": "<changes>\n### `engine/server/api/http_utils.py`\n- `respond_json` no longer sends any `access-control-*` header. The three lines are gone: allow-origin `*`, allow-methods and allow-headers. It still sends content-type and content-length. New docstring: \"Send a JSON response; the Engine sends no CORS headers (ADR-0004).\"\n- `respond_options` now answers a bare 204 (`send_response(204)` then `end_headers()`). Its four `access-control-*` lines are gone, max-age included. New docstring: \"Answer an OPTIONS request 204 with no CORS headers (ADR-0004).\"\n- Neither helper reads `Origin` or `server`. The Engine has no other place that writes headers.\n\n### `engine/server/api/server_config.py`\n- New `_resolve_flag_env(name) -> bool`, next to the other `_resolve_*_env` helpers. It returns true only when the variable, stripped and lower-cased, is `1`, `true` or `yes`. Any other value, blank or unset, gives false. It never raises.\n- `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED = _resolve_flag_env(\"RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG\")` replaces the literal `True`. The comment above it now names the variable. The flag is read once, when the module is imported. `server.py`, which passes it into `SimilarServer`, is unchanged.\n\n### `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py`\n- The `do_OPTIONS` docstring changes from \"Handle CORS preflight.\" to \"Answer OPTIONS 204 with no CORS headers.\" No behaviour changes: the existing 403 check in `_handle_similar` (`Debug mode is disabled`) now takes its value from the env-derived flag.\n\n### `tests/active/conftest.py`\n- The `engine` fixture adds `\"RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG\": \"1\"` to the env it gives the Engine process, after `**os.environ`, so a value exported in the shell cannot override it. The pytest process's own `os.environ` is untouched. Without this, every Engine-backed test that reads `debug.profile` (`test_profiles.py`) would get a 403 now that debug is off by default.\n\n### `tests/active/test_engine_response_defaults.py`, `tests/active/test_response_defaults.py`\n- Not created or edited in this step, same as in phase 1. This step asks only for the production code behind `tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase2.py`. I'm assuming the workflow promotes the durable tests from the checkpoint.\n\n### Hand-off\n- Any Engine started without `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1` now answers `?debug=1` on `/recommendations` and `/videos/similar` with 403 `Debug mode is disabled`, so `/videos.html?debug=1` shows that error until the variable is set.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase3.py": "<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>\n\n<items>\n<item id=\"C1b\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>Each ROUTES case now has an `expected` column holding the fixed text for that route, written as a literal. Line 165 asserts `json.loads(raw).get(\"error\") == expected`, where it used to check only for a non-empty string. The values come from the settled Step-5 table: likes-get and likes-import \u2192 \"Engine metadata failed\", block-add \u2192 \"Engine lookup failed\", action-resolve \u2192 \"Engine resolve failed\", action-centroids \u2192 \"Engine centroids failed\". likes-import uses \"metadata\", not today's \"resolve\" (draft departure 3). This excludes `\"error\"`, `\"EngineApiError\"`, a wrong operation name (e.g. \"Engine metadata failed\" on block-add, or \"Engine resolve failed\" on likes-import) and any string that keeps the `: {exc}` suffix. The run shows all five cases red at :165 against today's suffixed bodies, and each control at :163 passed.</what>\n</item>\n<item id=\"C1f\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>Line 180 now asserts `body[\"bridge_error\"] == BRIDGE_FIXED` (\"engine bridge unavailable\") on the dropped-connection path through POST /api/user-action. It used to check only for a non-empty string. This excludes `type(exc).__name__`, `str(exc)`, `repr(exc)` and any other string that changes with the cause. It also catches a fix that makes the URLError branch fixed but leaves the generic `except Exception` branch (where RemoteDisconnected lands) producing its own text. The run shows it red at :180, with 'Remote end closed connection without response' != 'engine bridge unavailable'.</what>\n</item>\n<item id=\"C1h\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>I added `test_user_action_bridge_http_error_carries_no_engine_text` (:185-195). A like is resolved (stub 200), then its publish meets the stub's default ingest reply of 500 `{\"error\": SENTINEL}`. Controls: :189 checks that both resolve and ingest were hit, and :190/:192 check the 502 and `bridge_ok` False. :194 asserts `bridge_error == \"engine bridge HTTP 500\"` exactly, and :195 asserts SENTINEL is absent from the raw body. This excludes a publish that reads the Engine's error body into `bridge_error`, in whole or appended. Before pinning the string I asked the operator, who answered \"Pin \\\"engine bridge HTTP 500\\\"\". R3 and the draft keep that fixed status string. A probe run showed today's value: 502, `\"bridge_error\": \"engine bridge HTTP 500\"`, no sentinel, no ERROR records. So this test is green before the phase. It guards a branch that already complies and is not a red for the phase. The docstring has a matching new bullet.</what>\n</item>\n</items>\n\n<findings_addressed>\nClaim CRITICAL 1 (C1b, :164): fixed. The per-route exact fixed text is now pinned at :165 from the settled Step-5 operation table, written as literals so the test states the spec rather than rebuilding production's f-string. Docstring bullet 2 narrowed to name each expected text.\nClaim CRITICAL 2 (C1f, :179): fixed. :180 is now `body[\"bridge_error\"] == BRIDGE_FIXED`. Docstring bullet 3 now says \"exactly `engine bridge unavailable`\".\nClaim CRITICAL 3 (C1h): fixed. The new test at :185-195 drives an ingest that answers 500 `{\"error\": SENTINEL}`, pins `bridge_error == \"engine bridge HTTP 500\"` (operator-confirmed) and asserts the sentinel is absent. The auditor read \"HTTP 500\" as Engine text. The operator and R3 settle that it is the Client's own fixed status string, and the Engine's actual text (the sentinel) is excluded at :195.\nShape RECOMMENDATION 1 (:164 and :179 check only non-empty): taken.     "step_7_implement:3": "<changes>\n### client/backend/server.py\n- New handler method `_respond_engine_failure(operation, exc)`. It logs one ERROR record with event `engine.call` and message `Engine <operation> failed`, carrying the request path and `str(exc)` as `context.error`, so the Engine's error text reaches the Client log (C2). It then answers 502 with exactly `{\"error\": \"Engine <operation> failed\"}` (C1).\n- All six Engine-call 502 sites now go through that method instead of putting `{exc}` in the body:\n  - `_handle_user_action` resolve \u2192 `resolve`\n  - `_handle_user_action` centroids \u2192 `centroids`\n  - `_handle_block_add` \u2192 `lookup`\n  - `_handle_user_profile_likes_get` \u2192 `metadata`\n  - `_handle_user_profile_likes_from_client` \u2192 `metadata`\n  - `_handle_likes_import` \u2192 `metadata`. This one used to say \"Engine resolve failed\", but the call it makes is the metadata call.\n- `_publish_to_engine_bridge`:\n  - **HTTPError:** still returns the fixed `engine bridge HTTP <code>`. It now also logs an ERROR `engine.bridge` record with the status and the Engine's response body as `context.error`.\n  - **Any other failure:** the `URLError`/`TimeoutError` branch and the `# pragma: no cover` `Exception` branch are now one `except Exception` branch. It logs an ERROR `engine.bridge` record with `str(exc)` as `context.error` and returns exactly `{\"ok\": False, \"error\": \"engine bridge unavailable\"}`. The merge is needed because urlopen wraps a refused connection in `URLError` but lets a dropped connection through unwrapped as `http.client.RemoteDisconnected`. The red run showed this: `bridge_error` was `Remote end closed connection without response`, so the old catch-all branch was the one being hit.\n\n### tests/active/test_response_defaults.py\nNot touched. The phase lists it as EDITED, but the file does not exist in the repo, and this phase's checkpoint is `tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase3.py`. Presumably the file gets created when the tmp checkpoints are promoted later. That step is out of scope here, so I didn't create it.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

The probe ran the planned similar and ingest ENGINE_PY children, with `configure_engine_logging(\"verbose\")` installed, against the current (pre-phase-4) code. The patched `_handle_random` path reaches the except branches, and today's bodies leak the exception text.\n- Similar stderr: every line was a JSON object from EngineJsonFormatter, including faiss's import-time logs (e.g. `{\"level\":\"INFO\",\"event\":\"engine.log\",\"message\":\"Loading faiss with AVX512 support.\",...}`). The probe file tests/tmp/test_probe_phase4.py is now a one-line \"spent, delete this file\" stub, as the phase-3 probe was, because I have no delete tool.\n</probes>\n\n<unassertable>\nnone\n</unassertable>",

ValidateTests: \"tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase4.py  3 failed\", \"[exit status 1]\", \"collected 3 items\", \"3 failed in 0.28s\".\n9. Red for the right reason \u2014 yes. Controls 140/173/177 passed; the statuses matched `[500]`. (c) Line 199: \"AssertionError: RuntimeError ... At index 1 diff: {'error': 'sentinel-ingest-5d7e'} != {'error': 'Event ingest failed'}\".
