### highest_risk


engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py (EngineJsonFormatter.format): the running Engine's only log formatter drops `record.exc_info`, so `logging.exception(...)` records only "server error", with no exception text and no traceback. Once the 500 bodies lose `str(exc)`, the cause disappears everywhere. A bare `ENGINE_PY` child test would still pass through `lastResort` and hide the gap. Fixing it touches the log format, which the brief lists as out of scope, so this needs a decision.
tests/active/conftest.py (engine fixture env, line 105): without `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1` in the session Engine's env, every `test_profiles.py` up-next test that reads `rows[0].debug.profile` through the Client proxy gets 403. The Engine's other debug consumers (the feed page's `?debug=1`) break the same way for anyone not opted in.
client/frontend/scripts/dev.mjs with client/frontend/src/data/api-base.ts: `npm run dev` always exports `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:7172`, and the page prefers it over its own origin, so the default dev setup is cross-origin and bypasses the Vite `/api` proxy. The plan's "default dev path may be unaffected" is wrong: every dev session fails until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` holds the exact browser origin (`http://localhost:5173` is not `http://127.0.0.1:5173`). Documenting `.env.bridge` as the place to set it, or `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG`, would also enable both in prod, because every unit shares that file.

## 2026-09-27 - Step 4 - Reassess the implementation plan (pass 1)

Pass 1. New impacts: YES.

I checked the inventory against the tree: `client/backend/lib/http_utils.py`, `engine/server/api/http_utils.py`, `client/backend/server.py` (constructor, `main()`, `_proxy_engine_request`, the six `EngineApiError` sites, `_publish_to_engine_bridge`), `client/backend/lib/engine_api_client.py`, `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py` (do_OPTIONS, do_GET/do_POST deadline wrappers, `_handle_similar`), `engine/server/api/handlers/internal_events.py`, `engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py`, `server_config.py`, `vite.config.ts`, `dev.mjs`, `api-base.ts`, and the tests' construction and env sites. Every entry I checked holds, down to the line numbers. A tree-wide grep for `str(exc)` and `{exc}` confirms that the plan's R3 site list is complete for 5xx bodies. A grep for `access-control` finds only the two `http_utils` modules. One small inaccuracy in the plan text: the Engine's `respond_json` has three `access-control-*` lines, not four; the inventory has it right.

The CORS, debug-flag and Client error-body parts of the plan work as designed. There is one real problem, and the inventory already points at it: the Engine error-logging half of R3 does not work in production as planned. `EngineJsonFormatter.format` builds its payload only from `record.getMessage()` and never reads `exc_info`. So the plan's `logging.exception(...)` records only "server error", with no exception text and no traceback, in the running Engine. The planned test runs a bare `ENGINE_PY` child without `configure_engine_logging`, so it would pass while production fails. That is a conflict between the settled plan and R3 and its acceptance criterion. Fixing it either touches the log format, which the requirements put out of scope, or changes the plan, so I report it as a conflict rather than work around it. I also found one new impact: `_post_json` wraps unexpected exceptions into `EngineApiError`, and the plan's `_respond_engine_failure` deliberately logs no traceback, so those unexpected failures lose theirs. Separately, the plan's hand-off note on `npm run dev` and its `/debug.html` reference are factually wrong against the tree.
<question id="1">
Partly. R1 (Client CORS), R2 (Engine CORS removal), R4 (debug flag) and the Client side of R3 work as planned. The getattr defaults make the Client helper safe for stubs. The trailing constructor parameter keeps `conftest.py:74,161` and `test_server.py:328` working. The `engine` fixture builds its env as `{**os.environ, ...}` (conftest.py:105), so adding `"RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG": "1"` there wins over anything the shell exports. The Engine side of R3 does not work as intended. The bodies become fixed, but `logging.exception` goes through `EngineJsonFormatter` (logging_profiles.py:187-223), which drops `exc_info`, so the production log has neither the exception nor the traceback. After this build the cause of an Engine 500 is recorded nowhere. The planned child-process test cannot detect this, because it runs without `configure_engine_logging`. One more gap: the six `EngineApiError` sites log no traceback, but `engine_api_client._post_json:62-63` also wraps unexpected exceptions, so R3's "traceback for unexpected ones" is not met there either.
</question>
<question id="2">
- **Callers see less.** The frontend and curl users see `Engine <op> failed` and `Engine read proxy failed` with no `detail`. The only reader of any of this is `.error`, so no code breaks, but the diagnostics now live only in the logs. For the Engine, that is only true once the formatter conflict is resolved.
- **Client log volume.** Transport failures, and the new `EngineApiError` and bridge logs, go to ERROR, which adds ERROR lines during an Engine outage. Nothing in the tree filters on level.
- **Dev workflow.** `dev.mjs:84-86,104` always exports `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:7172`, and `api-base.ts:19-21` prefers it over the page's own origin. So every `npm run dev` session is cross-origin, bypasses the Vite `/api` proxy, and fails until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` holds the exact origin the browser shows. `vite.config.ts` sets no host, so that origin is usually `http://localhost:5173`, not the plan's `http://127.0.0.1:5173`.
- **Debug off everywhere.** The feed page's `?debug=1` gets 403 on any Engine not opted in.
- **Shared `.env.bridge`.** Documenting it as the place for these variables would switch both on for the prod units too, because they share that file.
- **Timeouts inside handlers.** A statement-deadline `interrupted` error inside `_handle_similar` or the ingest handler keeps answering 500 instead of the outer 503. The body becomes fixed, and after the change a traceback is logged for a timeout.
</question>
<question id="3">
- **Engine log.** It must actually carry the exception and traceback, and the test must exercise the formatter production uses. Either render `exc_info` in `EngineJsonFormatter`, or put `traceback.format_exc()` into the message at the two Engine sites, and install `configure_engine_logging` in the test child. This is the conflict below.
- **`conftest.py:105`.** Add `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1` there, or every `test_profiles.py` up-next test gets 403.
- **Header tests.** The CORS tests need their own Client server built with the eighth argument, plus a raw `http.client` helper, because `ClientBackend.request` discards headers.
- **Docs.** DEPLOYMENT.md must use the exact browser origin and warn about `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1` and other ports. It must prefer per-unit drop-ins over the shared `.env.bridge`. It must reword the section 3b symptom `Engine metadata failed (HTTP 401)`, since the body no longer carries the status, and drop the nonexistent `/debug.html`.
- Nothing else in the tree needs to change for existing behaviour to keep working.
</question>
<question id="4">
- **Client CORS.** It goes from `*` on every response to nothing unless `Origin` exactly matches a configured entry. With a match it echoes the origin and adds `Vary: Origin`, plus max-age on preflight.
- **Engine CORS.** The Engine sends no CORS headers at all. OPTIONS answers a bare 204.
- **Client 502 bodies.** They lose `detail` and the `: <EngineApiError text>` suffix. `bridge_error` becomes `engine bridge unavailable` for transport and unexpected failures.
- **Engine 500 bodies.** They become fixed. A `ValueError` outside the three bad-request texts now gets a fixed 500 instead of its own text.
- **Client log levels.** The transport-unavailable log moves from WARNING to ERROR.
- **Debug.** `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED` defaults to off; `1`, `true` or `yes` turns it on.
- **Unchanged:** all 4xx messages, status codes, the `code` fields, the proxy's pass-through of Engine payloads, and the fixed `engine bridge HTTP {code}` and activitypub strings.
</question>

New impacts:
client/backend/lib/engine_api_client.py `_post_json` generic `except Exception` (62-63): it wraps unexpected failures into `EngineApiError(str(exc))`. Examples: a `json.JSONDecodeError` from a non-JSON 200 body at line 45, or `http.client.RemoteDisconnected` / `ConnectionResetError` when the Engine drops the connection on an uncaught exception. The plan's `_respond_engine_failure` deliberately logs no traceback ("an EngineApiError is an anticipated failure"), so these unexpected cases reach the Client log as one line of text with no traceback, short of R3's "with traceback for unexpected ones". `traceback.format_exc()` called inside the handler's except block includes the chained cause, so adding it to the `_respond_engine_failure` context would cover these cases.

Inventory entries that did not hold up:
none

Conflicts: Settled plan R3 (Engine) vs settled requirement R3 and its acceptance criterion "the Engine log carries the traceback", with "Logging format" out of scope. The plan logs through `logging.exception(...)` at `similar.py:1008-1018` and `internal_events.py:79-81`, and tests it in a bare `ENGINE_PY` child. But the running Engine's only root handler uses `EngineJsonFormatter.format` (`engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py:187-223`), which builds its payload from `record.getMessage()` alone and never renders `exc_info`. So production logs only "server error", with no exception and no traceback, while the child test passes through `logging.lastResort`. There are two ways to meet the requirement. (a) Render `exc_info` in the formatter. That edits the logging format, which is out of scope, so the requirements must allow it. (b) Log `traceback.format_exc()` explicitly in the message at the two sites. That changes the settled plan's R3 design. Either way, the plan's test for this criterion must install `configure_engine_logging` in the child, or it proves nothing about production.
Settled plan's Risks and R5 text vs the tree. (1) The hand-off note says "the default `npm run dev` path may be unaffected; only an explicit `--client-api-base` needs the variable". That is false: `client/frontend/scripts/dev.mjs:84-86,104` always exports `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE` (default `http://127.0.0.1:7172`), and `client/frontend/src/data/api-base.ts:19-21` prefers it, so every default dev session is cross-origin and breaks until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` is set. Because `vite.config.ts` sets no host, the origin the browser shows is typically `http://localhost:5173`, which the plan's example `http://127.0.0.1:5173` does not match under exact matching. (2) R5 says the flag "enables `?debug=1` for `/debug.html`", but no `debug.html` exists under `client/frontend/`; the debug view is the feed page with `?debug=1`.

Recommendations: 1. **Resolve the Engine logging conflict with option (b).** At the two Engine sites, log at ERROR with the exception and `traceback.format_exc()` in the message (e.g. `logging.error("[similar-server] server error: %s\n%s", exc, traceback.format_exc())`), and keep the fixed 500 bodies. The new test's child must call `configure_engine_logging` before it runs, so it asserts on the JSON line production actually emits.
   - Cost: the message is multi-line, so `_PREFIX_RE` (no DOTALL) does not match it and the event name falls back to `engine.log`. `_extract_fields` may also pull stray `key=value` tokens out of the traceback. Visibility is unaffected, because `payload_visible_in_mode` shows every ERROR line.
   - Alternative (a): add a `traceback` key from `self.formatException(record.exc_info)` in `EngineJsonFormatter`. It is cleaner and also fixes the existing `internal_events.py:116` gap. Cost: the operator must allow a log-format change that the requirements put out of scope, and `test_logging_profiles.py` must be re-run.
2. **Log a traceback in `_respond_engine_failure`.** Add `traceback.format_exc()` to its `_emit_client_log` context, or add it only when `exc.__cause__` is not a `URLError`/`TimeoutError`. Cost: one context key and longer ERROR lines during an Engine outage. It closes the new impact above.
3. **Raise the no-payload HTTPError log in `_proxy_engine_request` (664-676) from WARNING to ERROR when `exc.code >= 500`, and log `_publish_to_engine_bridge`'s `HTTPError` branch at ERROR.** Cost: two small edits and more ERROR lines. Both make "every 5xx/502 is logged at error level" literally true. Neither is in the plan today.
4. **Optionally, in both Engine catch-alls, re-raise `sqlite3.OperationalError` when `is_interrupted_error(exc)` holds,** so the outer do_GET/do_POST handler answers 503 `Query time limit exceeded` instead of a 500 with a traceback logged for a timeout. Cost: a status change from 500 to 503 for timeouts, which the plan did not scope. The body is fixed text either way, so it is not needed for R3.
5. **Correct the plan's hand-off and R5 text.**
   - Say that `npm run dev` is always cross-origin, so `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` must hold the exact page origin: `http://localhost:5173` or `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, depending on which URL is opened, plus any `--port` variant.
   - Drop `/debug.html` in favour of the feed page with `?debug=1`.
   - Prefer a per-unit systemd drop-in over the shared `.env.bridge` for both variables.
   - Cost: documentation only.
6. **Choose the ingest 500 message.** R3 asks for a fixed message that names the operation, so `Event ingest failed` fits better than `Internal server error` for `internal_events.py`. Cost: none; the Client sees only the status code there.

<impact path="client/backend/lib/http_utils.py" element="respond_json (33-42), respond_bytes (45-58), respond_options (61-68), and a new private CORS header helper">
**What changes.**
- The hard-coded `access-control-allow-origin: *`, allow-methods and allow-headers lines are removed from all three writers: 38-40, 54-56 and 64-67, where 67 is `max-age`.
- One private helper is called between `send_response` and `_finish_response`. `_finish_response` (20-30) is what calls `end_headers`.
- The helper reads `Origin` through `getattr(handler, "headers", None)` and the set through `getattr(getattr(handler, "server", None), "cors_origins", frozenset())`.
- On an exact match it sends the echoed allow-origin, `Vary: Origin`, allow-methods `GET, POST, OPTIONS` and `ALLOWED_REQUEST_HEADERS` (line 12, which stays), plus `access-control-max-age: 600` for `respond_options` only.
- `respond_options` still sends 204 with no body.
- The docstrings "with CORS headers" (34, 51) and "Respond to CORS preflight requests" (62) stop being accurate once no origin is configured.

**What depends on it.**
- `client/backend/server.py:33-34` imports all three.
- About 40 `respond_json` calls in server.py, including every 429, 401 and 400.
- `respond_bytes` for proxied Engine pages (604, 636) and the two 204s (345 profile delete, 981 block remove).
- `do_OPTIONS` (260-262).
- `tests/active/conftest.py:40` imports `RateLimiter` from this module (unchanged).
- The browser's cross-origin dev fetches depend on these headers (see the dev.mjs entry).

**Regression risk: medium.**
- (a) The header lookup must be case-insensitive. A real `HTTPMessage` is; a dict-headers stub would miss `Origin` and send no CORS, which is harmless.
- (b) The helper must run before `_finish_response`, because any header sent after `end_headers` is lost silently.
- (c) The body-less `respond_bytes(self, 204, b"")` still goes through the helper.
- (d) `Origin` is echoed only after exact membership in an operator-set frozenset, so no request-controlled value reaches a header unless it equals a configured one. That rules out header injection.
- (e) No test in `tests/active` asserts on `access-control-*` today (grep of `tests/`, empty), so every coverage test is new.
- (f) The Node-run frontend tests (`test_frontend_*.py`, which stub `window.location.origin` at lines 30-63 and bundle with `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE`) use Node fetch, which does not enforce CORS. I believe it also sends no `Origin`, but I have not verified that for undici. Either way they are unaffected.
</impact>
<impact path="client/backend/server.py" element="new module-level parse_cors_origins, beside parse_trusted_proxies (150-167)">
**What changes.** A new pure function:
- splits the value on commas, strips each entry, and drops empty entries and `*`;
- returns a `frozenset[str]`;
- raises nothing and validates nothing;
- unlike `parse_trusted_proxies`, has no default fallback.

**What depends on it.** Only `main()` and the new tests.

**Regression risk: low.**
- It must not be called at module level. `DEFAULT_TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS = parse_trusted_proxies(...)` at 167 does that for its own function, and copying the shape would break "never read at import".
- Note that `DEFAULT_CLIENT_PUBLISH_MODE` (line 50) already reads the env at import. That is a precedent to avoid here.
- The `*`-drop is the one behaviour beyond the stated parsing rules. The plan justifies it by the never-`*` invariant, and it needs its own test.
</impact>
<impact path="client/backend/server.py" element="ClientBackendServer.__init__ (202-224)">
**What changes.** A trailing `cors_origins: frozenset[str] = frozenset()` goes after `trusted_proxies` (213), stored as `self.cors_origins`.

**What depends on it.** These construct the server positionally:
- `main()` at 1183-1191, seven args;
- `tests/active/conftest.py:74` (`client_backend`) and `:161` (`_engine_client`), six args each;
- `tests/active/test_server.py:328` (`_client_backend`, also used by the `rig` fixture at 442), six args.

The new http_utils helper reads the attribute through `handler.server`.

**Regression risk: low.** The default keeps every six-argument caller working with no CORS. The parameter must go last: inserting it before `trusted_proxies` would silently bind the parsed networks to the wrong name in `main()`. A new test that wants CORS on must pass the eighth argument (or a keyword); no existing fixture allows it.
</impact>

<impact path="client/backend/server.py" element="_proxy_engine_request HTTPError branches (631-678), not in the plan">
**What changes.** Nothing, by the plan.

**Why it is listed.**
- (1) **The no-payload HTTPError path (663-678)** answers `int(exc.code)`, which can be a 5xx, with the fixed `Engine read proxy HTTP {code}`. It logs at `logging.WARNING`. The body is already fixed, but R3 says every 5xx is logged at error level. Step 4 should decide whether to log at ERROR when `exc.code >= 500`. My reading is that the requirement is ambiguous here.
- (2) **The HTTPError-with-payload path (632-662)** passes the Engine's error body and status through verbatim (`respond_bytes` with the Engine's content-type), logging only at INFO. Every Engine 5xx body therefore reaches the browser unchanged, so R3 depends entirely on the Engine sites below being fixed at source. It also means an Engine 403 `Debug mode is disabled` or a 400 reaches the browser as-is (intended).

**Regression risk: none if left alone.** The gap is completeness against R3.
</impact>
<impact path="client/backend/server.py" element="six EngineApiError handlers: _handle_user_action resolve (765-767) and centroids (794-796), _handle_likes_import (896-898), _handle_block_add lookup (958-960), _handle_user_profile_likes_get metadata (1014-1016), _handle_user_profile_likes_from_client metadata (1029-1031); new private handler method _respond_engine_failure">
**What changes.** Each `respond_json(self, 502, {"error": f"Engine … failed: {exc}"})` becomes `self._respond_engine_failure(operation, exc)`, which:
- logs at ERROR through `_emit_client_log` with the operation, `self.path` and `str(exc)`;
- answers 502 `{"error": f"Engine {operation} failed"}`.

The operation words keep today's text: `resolve`, `centroids`, `resolve`, `lookup`, `metadata`, `metadata`. `_handle_likes_import` (897) says "resolve" although, since plan 14, it calls `fetch_metadata_for_entries` (895). Keeping "resolve" limits the change to dropping the suffix, but "metadata" would be the accurate word, and Step 4 should pick one.

**What depends on it.**
- The frontend shows `payload.error`: `client/frontend/src/data/reactions.ts:43,79`, `blocks.ts:65`, `profile.ts:96`, `user-profile.ts:83`, `user-actions.ts:35`. The visible text loses its `: Engine … (HTTP n): …` suffix.
- `tests/active/test_dislikes.py:77` and `test_profiles.py:318` assert status only.
- The `rig` stub Engine in `test_server.py:403-445` is the ready harness for a forced metadata failure: its `/internal/videos/metadata` branch can return a 500 with a distinctive string.
- `DEPLOYMENT.md:227` quotes `Engine metadata failed (HTTP 401)` as a symptom (docs entry).

**Regression risk: low for behaviour, medium for logging completeness.**
- `EngineApiError` from `_post_json:62-63` also wraps unexpected exceptions, such as a `JSONDecodeError` on a non-JSON 200 body at line 45, or `RemoteDisconnected`. The plan logs no traceback, so these unexpected failures lose theirs. That falls short of R3's "traceback for unexpected ones". `traceback.format_exc()` inside the handler's except block would include the chained cause.
- For caplog: `_emit_client_log` serialises with `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=True)`. A test's distinctive Engine string should be plain ASCII with no quotes or backslashes, so it survives escaping.
- caplog sees ERROR records because the root logger defaults to WARNING and `logging.basicConfig` runs only in `main()`.
</impact>

<impact path="engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py" element="EngineJsonFormatter.format (184-223) and configure_engine_logging (226-238); not in the plan">
**What changes.** Nothing, by the plan.

**Why it is listed; I rate it the highest risk.**
- `configure_engine_logging` is called at `engine/server/api/server.py:324`. It clears the root handlers and installs `EngineJsonFormatter` as the only one.
- `format` builds its payload from `record.getMessage()` alone (189). It never reads `record.exc_info` or `exc_text`, and never calls `formatException`.
- So `logging.exception("server error")` in the running Engine emits only `{"level":"ERROR","message":"server error",...}`, with no exception text and no traceback.
- Once the 500 bodies stop carrying `str(exc)`, the cause of an Engine 500 is recorded nowhere. That contradicts R3 and the criterion "the Engine log carries the traceback".
- A test in a bare `ENGINE_PY` child that never calls `configure_engine_logging` falls back to `logging.lastResort`, whose default formatter does print the traceback. Such a test passes while production does not.

**Options.**
- (1) Render `exc_info` in the formatter, for example as a `traceback` key via `self.formatException`. This changes the log format, which the brief lists as out of scope, so it needs a ruling.
- (2) At the two sites, log `traceback.format_exc()` in the message. The message becomes multi-line, so `_PREFIX_RE` (17, no DOTALL) still matches the first line's `[scope]`. `_extract_fields` (108-124) will, however, pull stray `key=value` tokens out of the traceback. This is harmless but noisy. Visibility is unaffected, because WARNING and above go to every mode (`_classify_event`, 174-175).

**What depends on it.**
- `engine/server/api/tests/test_logging_profiles.py` builds records without `exc_info`, and it is not in `tests/active`, so `validate_tests.py` does not collect it.
- `internal_events.py:116` loses its traceback today for the same reason.

**Regression risk (if option 1 is taken).** It could shift `test_logging_profiles.py` expectations if the payload shape changes. Adding a key should not break them.
</impact>

### highest_risk

engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py EngineJsonFormatter.format (184-223): the production Engine's only log formatter, installed at server.py:324, builds its JSON from `record.getMessage()` and never renders `exc_info`. So the plan's `logging.exception(...)` at similar.py:1008-1018 and internal_events.py:79-81 records only "server error". Once the bodies lose `str(exc)`, the cause of an Engine 500 is logged nowhere. A bare `ENGINE_PY` child test passes through `logging.lastResort`, which does print the traceback, so the test goes green while production is wrong. Fixing it touches either the log format (out of scope) or the plan's R3 design, so it needs a decision.
tests/active/conftest.py engine fixture env (line 105): without `"RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG": "1"` in the session Engine's env, every `test_profiles.py` up-next test fails its 200 check in `_upnext_profile` (274-279) with a 403. The fixture is session-scoped and shared by every Engine-backed file, so the debug-off path cannot be tested through it, and the env-to-`SimilarServer` wiring is proven end-to-end only via `main()`.
client/frontend/scripts/dev.mjs with src/data/api-base.ts and client/backend/lib/http_utils.py: `npm run dev` always exports `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:7172`, and the page prefers it over its own origin. Every default dev session is therefore cross-origin and loses all API access once the wildcard goes, until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` holds the exact origin the browser shows. That is usually `http://localhost:5173`, not the plan's `127.0.0.1`. The plan's hand-off note says the opposite. Documenting `.env.bridge` as the place to set this or `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG` would also turn both on for prod, because every unit in one tree shares that file.

New impacts:
client/backend/server.py: the `ENGINE_PROXY_INVALID` 502 in `_proxy_engine_request` (598-600) answers a fixed body but logs nothing. With R3's "every 5xx logged at error level" it needs an ERROR `_emit_client_log` (method, path, status 502) before the respond; the plan does not name it.

Inventory entries that did not hold up:
none

Conflicts: R3 requirement ("the Engine log carries the traceback" for unexpected exceptions) vs settled plan R3 for `similar.py`/`internal_events.py`, which relies on `logging.exception`. In production the only root handler, installed by `configure_engine_logging` (engine `server.py:324`), uses `EngineJsonFormatter.format` (`logging_profiles.py:187-223`), which never renders `exc_info`. So the plan as written records no exception text or traceback, and the fix touches either the log format (out of scope per the brief) or the plan's logging mechanism.
Settled plan "Risks and gotchas" hand-off note ("the default `npm run dev` path may be unaffected; only an explicit `--client-api-base` needs the variable") vs the tree: `client/frontend/scripts/dev.mjs:84-86,104` always exports `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE` (default `http://127.0.0.1:7172`), and `client/frontend/src/data/api-base.ts:19-21` prefers it. Every default dev session is therefore cross-origin and breaks until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` is set, and the plan's example origin `http://127.0.0.1:5173` does not match the `http://localhost:5173` Vite usually shows.
Settled plan R5 ("enables `?debug=1` for `/debug.html`"; set via `.env.bridge`) vs the tree and the requirements. No `debug.html` exists under `client/frontend` (the debug view is `videos.html?debug=1`). `.env.bridge` is read by prod and dev units alike (`client/install-client-service.sh:196`, `engine/install-engine-service.sh:182`, `scripts/run-services.sh:90-93`), so documenting it as the place to set `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG`/`CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` undermines "debug off by default" and "unset in production".

Recommendations: 1. Engine traceback (resolves conflict 1). Option (a): at the two Engine sites, log `traceback.format_exc()` inside the message, e.g. `logging.error("[similar-server] server error: %s", traceback.format_exc())`. This leaves the format alone. The cost is multi-line `message` values, and `_extract_fields` may pull stray `key=value` context out of the traceback. Option (b): add a `traceback` key in `EngineJsonFormatter.format` when `record.exc_info` is set. That is about three lines, fixes `internal_events.py:116` too, and adds one key without breaking `test_logging_profiles.py`, but it is a log-format change the brief put out of scope. I recommend (b) if the operator accepts it as additive; otherwise (a). Either way, the new test must install `configure_engine_logging` in the child and assert on its output, or it proves nothing about production. Cost of the test change: one extra line in the child.
2. `EngineApiError` sites. In `_respond_engine_failure`, include `traceback.format_exc()` in the ERROR context. It carries the chained cause (JSONDecodeError, RemoteDisconnected). The cost is longer log lines on every Engine 4xx/5xx relay; the body stays unchanged.
3. Unlogged 502s. Add ERROR `_emit_client_log` calls at 598, 777 and the bridge HTTPError branch (1049-1050), and raise the no-payload HTTPError log (665) to ERROR when `exc.code >= 500`. The cost is four small log calls and no behaviour change, and it makes "every 5xx logged" literally true. If the operator reads R3 as covering only exception-bearing sites, skip this.
4. Operation word. Use `metadata`, not `resolve`, for `_handle_likes_import` (897), because since plan 14 it calls `fetch_metadata_for_entries`. The cost is one visible string change.
5. Timeouts. Leave `OperationalError('interrupted')` inside `similar.py`'s catch-all as a fixed 500 (pre-existing mis-routing). Re-raising it to get the outer 503 changes status and is beyond scope. The cost of leaving it is a traceback logged for each timeout.
6. `internal_events.py` body. Use `Event ingest failed` as the fixed 500 text so it names the operation. This costs nothing; the Client never reads that body.
7. Hand-off and DEPLOYMENT.md (conflicts 2 and 3). Correct the hand-off: default `npm run dev` needs `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173` (plus `http://127.0.0.1:5173` or the `--port` origin if used). Replace `/debug.html` with `/videos.html?debug=1` in section 7 (line 414 too), and recommend per-unit drop-ins (`systemctl edit peertube-client-dev` / `peertube-engine-dev`) or shell exports, mentioning `.env.bridge` only with the shared-file caveat. The cost is doc wording only.
8. Tests. Keep the live-Engine no-CORS test in its own file and `validate_tests.py` invocation. Strip `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG` from the child env in the unset-value flag tests. The cost is one extra test file and a `config.json` entry at harvest.

### impacts


<impact path="client/backend/lib/http_utils.py" element="respond_json (33-42), respond_bytes (45-58), respond_options (61-68), plus a new private CORS header helper">
**What changes.**
- The hard-coded `access-control-*` lines are removed:
  - three in `respond_json` (38-40);
  - three in `respond_bytes` (54-56);
  - four in `respond_options` (64-67; line 67 is `max-age: 600`).
- One private helper is called in each writer after `send_response` and before `_finish_response` (20-30). `_finish_response` is what calls `end_headers`.
- The helper reads `Origin` through `getattr(handler, "headers", None)` and the set through `getattr(getattr(handler, "server", None), "cors_origins", frozenset())`.
- On an exact match it sends:
  - the echoed `access-control-allow-origin`;
  - `Vary: Origin`;
  - allow-methods `GET, POST, OPTIONS`;
  - `ALLOWED_REQUEST_HEADERS` (line 12, which stays);
  - `access-control-max-age: 600`, from `respond_options` only.
- `respond_options` still sends 204 with no body.
- Three docstrings become inaccurate and need rewording: "Send a JSON response with CORS headers" (34), "…with CORS headers" (51) and "Respond to CORS preflight requests" (62).

**What depends on it.**
- `client/backend/server.py:33-34` imports all three writers.
- Every response in server.py goes through them, about 40 `respond_json` sites, including every 429, 401, 400 and 404.
- `respond_bytes` is used for:
  - proxied Engine pages (604, 636);
  - the two 204s: profile delete (345) and block remove (981).

<impact path="client/backend/server.py" element="_proxy_engine_request HTTPError branches (631-678) and ENGINE_PROXY_INVALID 502 (594-600); not named by the plan">
**What changes.** Nothing, according to the plan.

**Why it is listed.** R3 says every 5xx is logged at error level. Three sites fall short:
- **HTTPError with a payload (632-662).** It passes the Engine's status and body through verbatim with `respond_bytes`, logging only at INFO. Any Engine 5xx body therefore reaches the browser unchanged, so R3 depends entirely on the Engine sites below being fixed at the source. Unhandled Engine exceptions produce no body at all; they close the socket.
- **HTTPError without a payload (663-678).** It answers the upstream code, which can be a 5xx, with the fixed text `Engine read proxy HTTP {code}`, logged at WARNING.
- **`ENGINE_PROXY_INVALID` (598-600).** It answers a fixed 502 and logs nothing.

**Regression risk: none if left alone.** It is a completeness gap against a literal reading of R3, and whether to fix it is a scope decision. Raising these to ERROR would not change any response.
</impact>

<impact path="engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py" element="EngineJsonFormatter.format (184-223) and configure_engine_logging (226-238); not in the plan">
**What changes.** Nothing, by the plan.

**Why it is listed.**
- `configure_engine_logging` (called at `engine/server/api/server.py:324`) clears the root handlers and installs `EngineJsonFormatter` as the only one.
- `format` builds its payload from `record.getMessage()` alone (189). It never reads `record.exc_info` or `exc_text`, and never calls `formatException`.
- So in the running Engine, `logging.exception("server error")` emits `{"level":"ERROR","message":"server error",…}` with no exception text and no traceback.
- Once the 500 bodies lose `str(exc)`, the cause of an Engine 500 is recorded nowhere. That contradicts R3 and the criterion "the Engine log carries the traceback".
- An `ENGINE_PY` child test that never calls `configure_engine_logging` falls back to `logging.lastResort`, which does print the traceback. It passes while production fails.

**Options.**
- (a) Put `traceback.format_exc()` in the message at the two sites. This leaves the format alone, but `_extract_fields` may lift stray `key=value` tokens from the traceback.
- (b) Add a `traceback` key in `format` when `exc_info` is set. This also fixes `internal_events.py:116`, but it is a log-format change, which the brief lists as out of scope.

**What depends on it.** `engine/server/api/tests/test_logging_profiles.py`, which is not collected by `tests/active`.

**Regression risk: high for meeting R3; low for code if (b) only adds a key.**
</impact>

Conflicts: Plan R3 (Engine) vs requirement R3 and acceptance criterion "the Engine log carries the traceback", constrained by Out of scope "Logging format". The plan meets the Engine traceback requirement with `logging.exception` in `similar.py` (the existing `logging.exception("server error")` plus a new one for non-bad-request `ValueError`s) and in `internal_events.py`. But the running Engine's only handler is `EngineJsonFormatter` (`engine/server/api/logging_profiles.py:184-238`, installed at `engine/server/api/server.py:324`), and it serialises only `record.getMessage()`, dropping `exc_info`. So once the bodies stop carrying `str(exc)`, the cause of an Engine 500 is recorded nowhere in production. The plan's `ENGINE_PY` test would pass via `logging.lastResort` while production fails. There are two ways to satisfy R3. (a) Put `traceback.format_exc()` into the logged message at those sites. That changes the text of the "existing `logging.exception("server error")` stays" call R3 names, or adds a second log call beside it. (b) Have the formatter emit a `traceback` key when `exc_info` is set, which is a logging-format change the requirements put out of scope. The operator must choose which settled text gives.

Recommendations: 1. Resolve the conflict with option (a). At the three Engine sites (the `similar.py` non-bad-request `ValueError`, the `similar.py` catch-all, and the `internal_events.py` catch-all), keep `logging.exception(...)` and include the traceback text in the message, e.g. `logging.exception("[similar] server error\n%s", traceback.format_exc())`, with `import traceback` added to both files. It changes what: about three lines and two imports, no format change, and R3 is met in production. Costs:
- The "server error" message text changes, so the operator must read R3's "stays" as "keeps a `logging.exception` call".
- `_extract_fields` may add a few stray `key=value` context entries from the traceback text, which is harmless noise.
- Under `lastResort` in tests the traceback prints twice.
- The acceptance test must run `configure_engine_logging` in its `ENGINE_PY` child and assert that the JSON `message` carries the sentinel and `Traceback`.

Option (b), the alternative, is about three lines in `EngineJsonFormatter.format`. It also fixes every other `logging.exception` in the Engine (e.g. `internal_events.py:116`), but it needs the operator to amend "Logging format" out of scope, and it adds a key to every error line.

2. In `_respond_engine_failure`, also log `traceback.format_exc()`, at least when `exc.__cause__` is not a `URLError`/`TimeoutError`. It changes what: R3's "traceback for unexpected ones" is met for exceptions `_post_json:62-63` wraps (non-JSON 200, `RemoteDisconnected`). Cost: one context key, and larger log lines on those failures only.

3. Log the bridge `HTTPError` branch (`server.py:1049-1050`) at ERROR through `_emit_client_log` with the status. It changes what: the 502 it causes becomes traceable, since today an Engine ingest 5xx leaves no Client log line. Cost: one call and one ERROR line per failed publish. The response is unchanged.

4. Name the `_handle_likes_import` operation "metadata", not "resolve", because it calls `fetch_metadata_for_entries`. Name the ingest catch-all message `Event ingest failed`, since R3 wants the operation named. Cost: a one-word deviation from how the requirements grouped the site, with no behaviour change.

5. Correct the hand-off and the DEPLOYMENT.md text, at doc-wording cost only:
- The default `npm run dev` IS cross-origin (`dev.mjs:84-86` plus `api-base.ts:19-21`), so every dev session needs `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- Document that the Vite page is usually opened at `http://localhost:5173`, which is a distinct exact origin from `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, and that a `--port 5175` run needs its own entry.
- Recommend a per-unit systemd drop-in (`systemctl edit peertube-client-dev` / the dev Engine unit) rather than the shared `.env.bridge` for both variables, because prod and dev units, and `run-services.sh`, all read that one file.
- In §7, point debug at `/videos.html?debug=1` rather than `/debug.html`, which does not exist. Leave the pre-existing line 414 alone, or fix it only if the operator wants it, since the frontend debug page is out of scope.

6. Optional: add the configured origins to the `service.start` log context in `main()`. Cost: one dict key. Benefit: an operator can confirm what is active.

7. Put live-Engine tests (Engine no-CORS, debug rows) in a separate file from the stub and child tests, so they run in their own `validate_tests.py` invocation. Cost: one extra test file and one `config.json` entry at harvest.

### Client: `client/backend/lib/http_utils.py`

```python
ALLOWED_REQUEST_HEADERS = "content-type, x-profile-key"
CORS_ALLOWED_METHODS = "GET, POST, OPTIONS"
# Seconds a browser may cache a preflight answer.
CORS_PREFLIGHT_MAX_AGE = "600"


def _send_cors_headers(handler: BaseHTTPRequestHandler, preflight: bool = False) -> None:
    """Send the CORS headers when the request's `Origin` is exactly one the server lists, and none otherwise.

    The origin set is read from `handler.server.cors_origins`, and a handler without a server, headers or that attribute sends none.
    """
    headers = getattr(handler, "headers", None)
    origin = headers.get("Origin") if headers is not None else None
    allowed = getattr(getattr(handler, "server", None), "cors_origins", frozenset())
    # `*` is refused here as well as in the parser, since a server can be built with any set.
    if not origin or origin == "*" or origin not in allowed:
        return
    handler.send_header("access-control-allow-origin", origin)
    handler.send_header("vary", "Origin")
    handler.send_header("access-control-allow-methods", CORS_ALLOWED_METHODS)
    handler.send_header("access-control-allow-headers", ALLOWED_REQUEST_HEADERS)
    if preflight:
        handler.send_header("access-control-max-age", CORS_PREFLIGHT_MAX_AGE)
```

The writers:
- **`respond_json`**, docstring "Send a JSON response, with CORS headers for a listed origin.": `send_response` → content-type → `_send_cors_headers(handler)` → content-length → `_finish_response`.
- **`respond_bytes`**, docstring "Send a non-JSON response payload, with CORS headers for a listed origin.": same order.
- **`respond_options`**, docstring "Answer an OPTIONS request 204, with the preflight CORS headers for a listed origin.": `send_response(204)` → `_send_cors_headers(handler, preflight=True)` → `_finish_response(handler)`.

Invariants:
- The helper runs before `_finish_response`, so no header is sent after `end_headers`.
- Only a value equal to an operator-configured entry is echoed.
- `allow-credentials` is never sent.
- The helper touches neither `datetime` nor the module's imports, so `test_profiles.py`'s monkeypatch of `http_utils.datetime` is unaffected.
- A dict-headers stub gets `.get("Origin")` → None → no CORS, which is harmless.

### Client: `client/backend/server.py`

**Parser**, placed directly after `parse_trusted_proxies` and before `DEFAULT_TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS`. It is never called at module level.
```python
def parse_cors_origins(value: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Parse a `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` value: comma-separated exact origins, each compared to a request's `Origin` as a plain string.

    Whitespace around entries and blank entries are dropped, and so is `*`, which would otherwise be echoed back to a request sending `Origin: *`.
    """
    entries = (entry.strip() for entry in value.split(","))
    return frozenset(entry for entry in entries if entry and entry != "*")
```

**New handler method**, placed after `_handle_user_profile_likes_from_client`:
```python
    def _respond_engine_failure(self, operation: str, exc: EngineApiError) -> None:
        """Log a failed Engine call with its cause at error level and answer 502 naming only the operation, so no Engine error text reaches the caller.

        Call it only inside the `except EngineApiError` block, where `traceback.format_exc()` still sees the exception.
        """
        context: dict[str, Any] = {"operation": operation, "path": self.path, "error": str(exc)}
        cause = exc.__cause__
        # A cause other than a transport failure is unexpected, e.g. a non-JSON 200 or a dropped connection, and its traceback is the only record of it.
        if cause is not None and not isinstance(cause, (URLError, TimeoutError)):
            context["traceback"] = traceback.format_exc()
        _emit_client_log(logging.ERROR, "engine.call", f"engine {operation} failed", context)
        respond_json(self, 502, {"error": f"Engine {operation} failed"})
```

Call sites. Each `respond_json(self, 502, {"error": f"Engine … failed: {exc}"})` becomes `self._respond_engine_failure("<op>", exc)` and keeps the `return` after it.

| `_handle_user_action` | `_store_reaction` | `"centroids"` |
| `_handle_likes_import` | `fetch_metadata_for_entries` | `"metadata"` (was "resolve"; this is the call it makes) |
| `_handle_block_add` | resolve and metadata | `"lookup"` |
| `_handle_user_profile_likes_get` | metadata | `"metadata"` |
| `_handle_user_profile_likes_from_client` | metadata | `"metadata"` |

  - None carries a header starting `access-control-`.
- **Debug on.** `POST /recommendations?debug=1&limit=3` → 200, and every row has a `debug` key. The fixture sets `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1`, so this proves env → `server_config` → `main()` → gate end to end.

### Docs

These follow the settled checklist:
- **DEPLOYMENT.md §7**: `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1`, off by default, `1`/`true`/`yes` in any case, 403 `Debug mode is disabled` otherwise. Point at `/videos.html?debug=1`, not `/debug.html`. Prefer a per-unit drop-in over the shared `.env.bridge`.
- **DEPLOYMENT.md §6**: a `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` paragraph:
  - exact origins; whitespace, blank entries and `*` are ignored;
  - unset in production;
  - `npm run dev` always targets `http://127.0.0.1:7172`, so default dev is cross-origin and needs this;
  - `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are distinct entries, and `--port 5175` needs its own;
  - a change needs a restart.
- **DEPLOYMENT.md §3b**: the `Engine metadata failed` symptom (the HTTP status is now only in `journalctl`).
- **Triage rows**, optional.
- **The three READMEs**, as listed in the checklist.
- No file quotes the `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED = True` constant any more.

### Departures from the high-level plan

1. **Engine formatter gains a `traceback` key.** This is operator decision (b). Without it, R3's "Engine log carries the traceback" is false in production.
2. **`_respond_engine_failure` logs a traceback when the `EngineApiError` wraps a non-transport cause.** The plan said no traceback. `_post_json` wraps unexpected exceptions (a non-JSON 200, `RemoteDisconnected`) into `EngineApiError`, and R3 wants a traceback for unexpected ones. Transport failures and HTTP-status failures stay traceback-free.
3. **The likes-import operation word is `metadata`, not `resolve`**, because that is the call it makes.
4. **The recommendations 500 message is `Recommendations request failed`, not `Internal server error`.** R3 requires the message to name the operation. The ingest message is `Event ingest failed` for the same reason.
5. **`_send_cors_headers` also refuses `Origin: *`**, as well as the parser dropping it. The constructor accepts any set, so the invariant is enforced where the header is sent.

### Deliberate simplifications and known limits

- **Exact-string origin match with no normalisation.** Ceiling: `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` need separate entries. Upgrade path: normalise both sides in the parser and the helper.
- **Origin set fixed for the process's life.** A change needs a restart, as with `TRUSTED_PROXIES`.
- **`Vary: Origin` only on a match.** With origins configured, a shared cache could serve a no-CORS response to a listed origin. This is accepted, since only local dev configures origins and nginx does not cache the API.
- **Not changed, by the plan's scope:**
  - The proxy HTTPError-without-payload branch still logs an upstream 5xx at WARNING.
  - `ENGINE_PROXY_INVALID` still logs nothing.
  - The bridge `engine bridge HTTP {code}` path still logs nothing.
  - All three bodies are already fixed text, and the Engine side logs its own 5xx with a traceback now. Raising these log levels is a follow-up if a strict reading of R3's logging clause is wanted.
- **Debug 403 without the variable is proven through an `ENGINE_PY` child**, which uses the imported `server_config` flag in a stub server. `main()`'s env-to-server wiring is proven only by the flag-on live test.
- **Pre-existing timeout behaviour.** An `OperationalError('interrupted')` inside `_handle_similar` or ingest still lands in the catch-all as a 500. It now has a fixed body and a logged traceback.

### Hand-off notes

- The Vite dev setup, including plain `npm run dev`, which always sets `VITE_CLIENT_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:7172`, gets no API access until `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` lists the page's exact origin.
- `/videos.html?debug=1` shows `Debug mode is disabled` until the Engine runs with `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1`.
- Neither variable should go in the shared `.env.bridge` on a host that also runs prod units; use a per-unit drop-in.
- Run `test_engine_response_defaults.py` in its own `validate_tests.py` invocation, because of the Engine rate limit.
- At harvest, add both new test files to `.un/skills/devsecops/config.json` and map `logging_profiles.py`.

Approved by the operator.

#### Phase 1 - Client CORS by exact origin [code]

**Files touched.** client/backend/lib/http_utils.py (EDITED), client/backend/server.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_response_defaults.py (NEW)

**Checkpoint.** Seam 1 is `parse_cors_origins` as a pure function: "" → empty; " http://a:1 , ,http://b " → {"http://a:1", "http://b"}; "*, http://a" → {"http://a"}; ",," → empty. Seam 2 is the HTTP boundary of a live Client. The test builds two `ClientBackendServer`s on ephemeral ports over a tmp users.db, the same construction as the `client_backend` fixture in tests/active/conftest.py plus the trailing `cors_origins` argument: one with frozenset() and one with frozenset({"http://127.0.0.1:5173"}). Both are read through raw `http.client` so every header is visible. Assertions: (a) With the empty set, GET /api/health and OPTIONS /api/user-profile carry no header starting `access-control-`, whatever the Origin, and OPTIONS is 204. (b) With the listed set, Origin http://127.0.0.1:5173 on a GET gets allow-origin echoed, `vary: Origin`, methods "GET, POST, OPTIONS", headers "content-type, x-profile-key", no max-age and no allow-credentials. (c) The same Origin on OPTIONS gets 204, the same headers, and max-age "600". (d) Origins http://localhost:5173, https://evil.example and `*` get no access-control-* header on GET or OPTIONS, and OPTIONS is still 204. (e) The 401 from GET /api/user-profile (respond_json) and the 204 from POST /api/profile/delete (respond_bytes) carry the echo. (f) No header value in any of these responses equals `*`.

**Intent.** The Client backend sends CORS headers only to a request whose Origin exactly matches the set that `parse_cors_origins` builds from CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS in `main()` and that `ClientBackendServer` holds as `cors_origins`.

- C1 - `parse_cors_origins` turns a CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS value into a frozenset of exact origins, dropping surrounding whitespace, blank entries and `*`.
- C2 - `respond_json`, `respond_bytes` and `respond_options` send access-control-* headers only when the request's Origin is in `server.cors_origins`: they echo that Origin with `Vary: Origin`, and they add max-age 600 only on the 204 preflight.

**Outcome.** _pending_

Needs coordination: No phase needs a credential or a manual step. The checkpoints for phases 2 and 4 run ENGINE_PY children and need the Engine pixi environment installed locally at engine/.pixi/envs/default/bin/python. Phase 2's live-Engine checkpoint, tests/active/test_engine_response_defaults.py, must run in its own validate_tests.py invocation because of the Engine rate limit.

Rationale: The build splits along the four settled requirements, turned into four seams, and each Intent reduces to two clauses. R1 (Client CORS) is its own phase: parsing in one clause, gated header emission in the other. R2 and R4 share a phase because both are Engine response defaults and are proven through the same Engine harnesses: server_config child imports, an ENGINE_PY child, and the live `engine` fixture, whose env change (RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1) must land together with the flag so that test_profiles.py stays green. R3 is split by service. Its Client half (fixed 502 and bridge_error text plus ERROR logging) is proven at the Client HTTP boundary with a stub Engine and caplog. Its Engine half (fixed 500s plus the formatter's traceback key, operator decision (b)) is proven in ENGINE_PY children running the production formatter. One R3 phase would have carried three or more facts across two services and two harnesses. R5 and the README edits are documentation, so they get no phase and are left to Step 9. The malformed-JSON 400 criterion is unchanged behaviour, so it sits in phase 3's checkpoint as a regression guard rather than as a clause. The step's {principles}, {shape_ladder-ladder} and {tdd_seams} placeholders arrived unfilled, so the seams were placed on the harnesses the tree already uses (the conftest fixtures, the test_similar.py ENGINE_PY children and the test_server_config.py `_run` pattern), which I confirmed by reading tests/active. ### `tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py` - 7058 characters, inlined in full

```
"""The Client backend sends CORS headers only to a request whose `Origin` is exactly one it lists.

- `parse_cors_origins` turns a `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` value into a frozenset of exact origins: surrounding whitespace, blank entries and `*` are dropped, and a value listing nothing is the empty set.
- A Client built with no origins answers GET /api/health and OPTIONS /api/user-profile with no `access-control-*` header, whatever the `Origin` (listed elsewhere, foreign, `*` or absent); OPTIONS is 204.
- A Client listing http://127.0.0.1:5173 answers that `Origin` on GET /api/health with exactly allow-origin (the origin echoed), allow-methods `GET, POST, OPTIONS` and allow-headers `content-type, x-profile-key`, plus `Vary: Origin`; no max-age and no allow-credentials. On OPTIONS it answers 204 with the same headers and max-age `600`.
- The same Client answers http://localhost:5173, https://evil.example, `*` and no `Origin` with no `access-control-*` header on GET or OPTIONS; OPTIONS is still 204.
- The 401 from GET /api/user-profile (`respond_json`) and the 204 from POST /api/profile/delete (`respond_bytes`) carry the same echo and `Vary: Origin`.
- No header value in any of these responses is `*`.

Each Client is a real `ClientBackendServer` on 127.0.0.1:0 over a tmp users.db, built as conftest's `client_backend` is plus the trailing `cors_origins`, and read through raw `http.client` so every header, duplicates included, is visible.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import http.client
import json
import sys
import threading
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
BACKEND_DIR = ROOT / "client" / "backend"
if str(BACKEND_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(BACKEND_DIR))

import server as client_server  # noqa: E402
from lib.http_utils import RateLimiter  # noqa: E402
from lib.users_store import ensure_user_schema  # noqa: E402

CLOSED_ENGINE = "http://127.0.0.1:9"
LISTED = "http://127.0.0.1:5173"
UNLISTED = ("http://localhost:5173", "https://evil.example", "*", None)
ECHO = {"access-control-allow-origin": [LISTED], "access-control-allow-methods": ["GET, POST, OPTIONS"], "access-control-allow-headers": ["content-type, x-profile-key"]}
PREFLIGHT_ECHO = {**ECHO, "access-control-max-age": ["600"]}


@contextmanager
def _client(tmp_path, cors_origins):
    """A Client backend on 127.0.0.1:0 as conftest's `client_backend` is built, plus `cors_origins`; yields its port."""
    conn = client_server.connect_db(tmp_path / "users.db")
    ensure_user_schema(conn)
    srv = client_server.ClientBackendServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), client_server.ClientBackendHandler, conn, CLOSED_ENGINE, "bridge", RateLimiter(1000, 60), cors_origins=cors_origins)
    thread = threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    try:
        yield srv.server_address[1]
    finally:
        srv.shutdown()
        srv.server_close()
        conn.close()


def _raw(port, method, path, origin, extra=None):
    """Send one request, with `Origin: origin` unless it is None; return the status, every header as lower-cased name -> list of values, and the body."""
    headers = dict(extra or {})
    if origin is not None:
        headers["Origin"] = origin
    conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=30)
    try:
        conn.request(method, path, body=b"" if method == "POST" else None, headers=headers)
        resp = conn.getresponse()
        body = resp.read()
        seen: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for name, value in resp.getheaders():
            seen.setdefault(name.lower(), []).append(value)
        return resp.status, seen, body
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _cors(headers):
    return {name: values for name, values in headers.items() if name.startswith("access-control-")}


def _star_values(responses):
    return [(name, value) for _, headers, _ in responses for name, values in headers.items() for value in values if value.strip() == "*"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("value", "expected"), [
    ("", frozenset()),
    (" http://a:1 , ,http://b ", frozenset({"http://a:1", "http://b"})),
    ("*, http://a", frozenset({"http://a"})),
    (",,", frozenset()),
])
def test_parse_cors_origins_keeps_exact_origins_only(value, expected):
    parsed = client_server.parse_cors_origins(value)
    assert isinstance(parsed, frozenset)  # C1
    assert parsed == expected  # C1


def test_no_listed_origin_sends_no_cors_headers(tmp_path):
    responses = []
    with _client(tmp_path, frozenset()) as port:
        for origin in (LISTED, *UNLISTED):
            got = _raw(port, "GET", "/api/health", origin)
            assert got[0] == 200
            assert _cors(got[1]) == {}, origin  # C2
            responses.append(got)
            got = _raw(port, "OPTIONS", "/api/user-profile", origin)
            assert got[0] == 204, origin  # C2
            assert _cors(got[1]) == {}, origin  # C2
            responses.append(got)
    assert _star_values(responses) == []  # C2


def test_listed_origin_is_echoed_with_vary_and_preflight_max_age(tmp_path):
    with _client(tmp_path, frozenset({LISTED})) as port:
        get = _raw(port, "GET", "/api/health", LISTED)
        preflight = _raw(port, "OPTIONS", "/api/user-profile", LISTED)
    assert get[0] == 200
    assert _cors(get[1]) == ECHO  # C2
    assert "access-control-max-age" not in get[1]  # C2
    assert "access-control-allow-credentials" not in get[1]  # C2
    assert get[1].get("vary") == ["Origin"]  # C2
    assert preflight[0] == 204  # C2
    assert _cors(preflight[1]) == PREFLIGHT_ECHO  # C2
    assert preflight[1].get("vary") == ["Origin"]  # C2
    assert _star_values([get, preflight]) == []  # C2


def test_unlisted_origin_gets_no_cors_headers(tmp_path):
    responses = []
    with _client(tmp_path, frozenset({LISTED})) as port:
        for origin in UNLISTED:
            got = _raw(port, "GET", "/api/health", origin)
            assert got[0] == 200
            assert _cors(got[1]) == {}, origin  # C2
            responses.append(got)
            got = _raw(port, "OPTIONS", "/api/user-profile", origin)
            assert got[0] == 204, origin  # C2
            assert _cors(got[1]) == {}, origin  # C2
            responses.append(got)
    assert _star_values(responses) == []  # C2


def test_error_and_bytes_responses_echo_listed_origin(tmp_path):
    with _client(tmp_path, frozenset({LISTED})) as port:
        refused = _raw(port, "GET", "/api/user-profile", LISTED)
        minted = _raw(port, "POST", "/api/profile", None)
        assert minted[0] == 201
        deleted = _raw(port, "POST", "/api/profile/delete", LISTED, {"X-Profile-Key": json.loads(minted[2])["key"]})
    assert refused[0] == 401
    assert _cors(refused[1]) == ECHO  # C2
    assert refused[1].get("vary") == ["Origin"]  # C2
    assert deleted[0] == 204
    assert _cors(deleted[1]) == ECHO  # C2
    assert deleted[1].get("vary") == ["Origin"]  # C2
    assert _star_values([refused, deleted]) == []  # C2

```

<changes>
### `client/backend/lib/http_utils.py`
- New private `_send_cors_headers(handler, preflight=False)`. It reads the request's `Origin` from the handler. If that Origin is exactly in `handler.server.cors_origins`, it sends: `access-control-allow-origin` set to that Origin, the existing allow-methods (`GET, POST, OPTIONS`) and allow-headers (`content-type, x-profile-key`), `access-control-max-age: 600` only when `preflight` is true, and `vary: Origin`. For any other Origin, or none, it sends no `access-control-*` header and no `Vary`.
- `respond_json` and `respond_bytes` no longer hard-code `access-control-allow-origin: *` and the allow-* headers. They call `_send_cors_headers(handler)` instead.
- `respond_options` still answers 204 but now calls `_send_cors_headers(handler, preflight=True)`, so max-age goes out only alongside an echoed Origin. Nothing in this module sends `*` any more.

### `client/backend/server.py`
- New `parse_cors_origins(value) -> frozenset[str]`, placed next to `parse_trusted_proxies`. It splits on commas, trims whitespace, and drops blank entries and `*`. Matching is exact: no case folding and no trailing-slash normalisation. A value listing nothing gives the empty set, so no origin is allowed.
- `ClientBackendServer.__init__` takes a new trailing argument, `cors_origins: frozenset[str] = frozenset()`, after `trusted_proxies`, and stores it as `self.cors_origins`. The existing six-argument construction (as in conftest's `client_backend`) holds the empty set.
- `main()` parses `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` from the environment right after `TRUSTED_PROXIES`, before the signal swap and the DB/bind, and passes the result to `ClientBackendServer`.
- For the hand-off: once this lands, the Vite dev setup gets no CORS headers until the Client backend is started with `CLIENT_CORS_ORIGINS` set to the Vite origin (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:5173`). This is by design under ADR-0004, and `DEPLOYMENT.md` documents it in a later phase.

Not created here. The phase list names it as NEW, but this step asks only for the production code behind the checkpoint `tests/tmp/test_15_tighten_response_defaults_phase1.py`. The durable test is expected to be promoted from that checkpoint by the workflow.
</changes>

```
"""The Engine sends no CORS header on any response, and serves recommendation debug metadata only when `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG` is 1, true or yes.

- `server_config` imported in a child whose `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG` is `1`, `true`, `yes`, `TRUE` or ` yes ` holds `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED` True; unset, `""`, `0`, `no` or `on` holds False.
- Under the Engine interpreter with `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG` unset, the real `SimilarHandler._handle_similar`, on a stub server whose `recommendations_debug_enabled` is the imported flag, answers `{"debug": ["1"]}` (with or without `random`) with exactly one `respond_json(handler, 403, {"error": "Debug mode is disabled"})` and serves nothing, while a request not asking for debug is served. With `RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG=1` the same debug request is served with debug included and nothing is refused.
- The live `engine` fixture from tests/active/conftest.py answers GET /api/health (200), OPTIONS /recommendations and /api/health (204), POST /recommendations (200), a malformed POST /recommendations (400) and an unknown route (404), each sent with `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:5173`, with no header starting `access-control-`.
- That Engine, started with the fixture's env, answers POST /recommendations?debug=1&limit=3 with 200 and three rows that each carry a `debug` object naming its profile; without `debug=1` no row carries `debug`.

The live checks run against the `engine` fixture imported from tests/active/conftest.py, so this file runs in its own validate_tests.py invocation because of the Engine rate limit.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import http.client
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ACTIVE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "active"
if str(ACTIVE_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ACTIVE_DIR))

from conftest import ENGINE_PY, ROOT, engine  # noqa: E402,F401

SERVER_DIR = ROOT / "engine" / "server"
API_DIR = SERVER_DIR / "api"
VAR = "RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG"
ORIGIN = "http://127.0.0.1:5173"
DISABLED = [True, 403, {"error": "Debug mode is disabled"}]
# repr so a flag left as the raw env string prints '1' and not True.
PRINT_FLAG = "import server_config as c; print(repr(c.RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED))"


def _env(value: str | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    # The value goes only into a copy for the child, so a shell that exports the variable cannot flip the unset case.
    env = {key: val for key, val in os.environ.items() if key != VAR}
    if value is not None:
        env[VAR] = value
    return env


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value, expected", [
    ("1", "True"),
    ("true", "True"),
    ("yes", "True"),
    ("TRUE", "True"),
    (" yes ", "True"),
    (None, "False"),
    ("", "False"),
    ("0", "False"),
    ("no", "False"),
    ("on", "False"),
], ids=["one", "true", "yes", "upper-true", "padded-yes", "unset", "empty", "zero", "no", "on"])
def test_flag_is_true_only_for_1_true_or_yes(value, expected):
    run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", PRINT_FLAG], cwd=API_DIR, env=_env(value), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)

    assert run.returncode == 0, run.stderr[-2000:]
    assert run.stdout.strip() == expected  # C2


# Runs under the Engine interpreter: importing handlers.similar needs numpy and faiss, which only its pixi env carries.
_DEBUG_CHILD = textwrap.dedent(
    """
    import json, sys, types
    from unittest.mock import patch
    sys.path[:0] = [sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]]
    import server_config
    from handlers import similar

    class Handler:
        def __init__(self):
            self.server = types.SimpleNamespace(default_limit=20, refresh_similarity_cache=False, recommendations_debug_enabled=server_config.RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED)
            self.served = []

        def _handle_random(self, limit, include_debug, request_id, started_at):
            self.served.append([limit, include_debug])

    out = {"flag": server_config.RECOMMENDATIONS_DEBUG_ENABLED, "cases": []}
    for params in json.loads(sys.argv[3]):
        handler = Handler()
        with patch.object(similar, "respond_json") as respond:
            similar.SimilarHandler._handle_similar(handler, params)
        out["cases"].append({"respond": [[c.args[0] is handler, *c.args[1:]] for c in respond.call_args_list], "served": handler.served})
    print(json.dumps(out))
    """
)


def _handle(value: str | None, cases: list[dict]) -> dict:
    assert ENGINE_PY.exists(), f"Engine interpreter missing at {ENGINE_PY}; run `pixi install` in engine/"
    run = subprocess.run([str(ENGINE_PY), "-c", _DEBUG_CHILD, str(SERVER_DIR), str(API_DIR), json.dumps(cases)], cwd=API_DIR, env=_env(value), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    assert run.returncode == 0, run.stderr[-2000:]  # control: the Engine's interpreter imported the handler and ran every case
    return json.loads(run.stdout)


def test_debug_request_is_refused_403_unless_the_flag_is_set():
    # Control: with the flag set, the same debug request reaches the (stubbed) random feed with debug included, and nothing is refused.
    enabled = _handle("1", [{"debug": ["1"], "random": ["1"]}, {"random": ["1"]}])
    assert enabled == {"flag": True, "cases": [{"respond": [], "served": [[20, True]]}, {"respond": [], "served": [[20, False]]}]}

    disabled = _handle(None, [{"debug": ["1"]}, {"debug": ["1"], "random": ["1"]}, {"random": ["1"]}])

    assert disabled["flag"] is False  # C2
    assert disabled["cases"][0] == {"respond": [DISABLED], "served": []}  # C2
    assert disabled["cases"][1] == {"respond": [DISABLED], "served": []}  # C2
    # The refusal is tied to asking for debug: the same handler with the flag off still serves a plain request.
    assert disabled["cases"][2] == {"respond": [], "served": [[20, False]]}


def _raw(engine, method: str, path: str, body: bytes | None = None) -> tuple[int, dict[str, list[str]], bytes]:
    """Send one request with `Origin: ORIGIN` to the Engine; return the status, every header as lower-cased name -> list of values, and the body."""
    port = int(engine.base.rsplit(":", 1)[1])
    headers = {"Origin": ORIGIN}
    if body is not None:
        headers["content-type"] = "application/json"
    conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=120)
    try:
        conn.request(method, path, body=body, headers=headers)
        resp = conn.getresponse()
        data = resp.read()
        seen: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for name, value in resp.getheaders():
            seen.setdefault(name.lower(), []).append(value)
        return resp.status, seen, data
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _cors(headers: dict[str, list[str]]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    return {name: values for name, values in headers.items() if name.startswith("access-control-")}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("method, path, body, status", [
    ("GET", "/api/health", None, 200),
    ("OPTIONS", "/recommendations", None, 204),
    ("OPTIONS", "/api/health", None, 204),
    ("POST", "/recommendations?limit=1", b"{}", 200),
    ("POST", "/recommendations", b"{not json", 400),
    ("GET", "/no-such-route", None, 404),
], ids=["health", "options-recommendations", "options-health", "recommendations", "malformed-json", "not-found"])
def test_no_engine_response_carries_a_cors_header(engine, method, path, body, status):
    got = _raw(engine, method, path, body)

    assert got[0] == status, got[2][:300]  # control: the request reached the route this case names
    # Control: headers are read off the wire; every Engine response carries Server and Date, and JSON ones carry content-type.
    assert "server" in got[1] and "date" in got[1], got[1]
    if status != 204:
        assert got[1].get("content-type") == ["application/json; charset=utf-8"], got[1]
    assert _cors(got[1]) == {}, got[1]  # C1


def test_engine_started_with_the_flag_returns_debug_rows(engine):
    status, body = engine.request("POST", "/recommendations?debug=1&limit=3", body={})

    assert status == 200, body  # C2
    assert len(body["rows"]) == 3, body
    for row in body["rows"]:
        assert isinstance(row.get("debug"), dict), row  # C2
        assert "profile" in row["debug"], row["debug"]  # C2

    # Control: the same request without debug=1 carries no `debug`, so the key above comes from the debug path.
    status, plain = engine.request("POST", "/recommendations?limit=3", body={})
    assert status == 200, plain
    assert len(plain["rows"]) == 3 and not any("debug" in row for row in plain["rows"]), plain["rows"]
```
